On this Veterans Day, President Donald J. Trump stood among the fallen at Arlington National Cemetery and rendered our nation’s highest salute to the living who still carry the cost of freedom. In words that echoed across the quiet hills where generations of heroes rest, the Commander-in-Chief honored every Patriot who has worn the uniform — from the beaches of Normandy to the mountains of Afghanistan — vowing that “while I’m President of the United States, we will always fulfill our duty to them.”

In a solemn and stirring address, President Trump saluted America’s warriors:

  • “On Veterans Day, we reaffirm our undying gratitude to every Patriot who has answered the call of duty. We pay tribute to all of those who have won the wars and worn the uniform, who face the enemy, who have beaten the enemy at every turn, who have borne the burdens of fate and destiny to stand as our protection in battle.” (Watch)
  • “We thank Almighty God for the noble warriors of the United States Military who have always stepped forward so that America might always stay free. To every veteran here at Arlington and across the nation: today we render you the highest salute, we offer you our deepest respect and love, and we pledge you our utmost loyalty and devotion.” (Watch)
  • “Across every generation, American liberty has been preserved by legions of selfless Patriots who have raised their right hands and sworn an oath of flesh and blood for a cause whose full cost could not be measured in advance… Time and time again for 250 years, the American warrior has returned victorious, our Republic has triumphed, and today, our country is stronger than it has ever been before.” (Watch)
  • “A nation without heroes is like a sky without stars or a heaven without angels — but in America, we’ve never known that darkness because we have the men and women of America’s armed forces, our guiding lights, our greatest heroes, and our guardian angels.” (Watch)
  • “From the Patriots’ first stand at Lexington Green and the Concord Bridge to the blood-soaked battlefields that saved our nation, from the treacherous trenches of Europe to the deepest waters of the Pacific and the farthest reaches of the world, our veterans have answered every call, met every threat, crushed every foe, and borne every burden of war so that our children might know every single blessing of peace and love.” (Watch)
  • “America’s veterans have always fulfilled their duty to us, and while I’m President of the United States, we will always fulfill our duty to them.” (Watch)
  • “We say to every American veteran: the sacrifice you have made, we will never forget; the oath that you have kept, we will never take for granted; the values you fought for, we will never, ever forsake; the flag you held high, we will never let it fall; and the nation you served, we will never, ever let it fail.” (Watch)

President Trump also recognized living legends whose service spans generations, each a living testament to American valor:

  • On Cpl. Jack Myers, World War II: “At 19 years old, Jack Myers kissed his young bride and newborn son goodbye and went to serve as a gunner in the 692nd Tank Destroyer Battalion in World War II — brave people, all. In the frostbitten winter of 1944, Cpl. Myers found himself in the largest battle in American history, the Battle of the Bulge… Months later, Jack’s battalion was among the first to liberate the Dachau concentration camp, coming face to face with the evil he risked his life to destroy. Today, Jack is a great-great-grandfather and is here to receive our nation’s gratitude at 103 years old.” (Watch)
  • On Col. Douglas Moore, Vietnam: “U.S. Army Col. Douglas Moore served as one of the famous Dustoff medevac pilots in Vietnam — boy, could they fly — flying an incredible 1,874 combat missions and evacuating 2,782 badly wounded soldiers… For his actions, Douglas received our military’s second-highest honor, the Distinguished Service Cross. Over three decades, he also received two Distinguished Flying Crosses, a Bronze Star, and 33 Air Medals.” (Watch)
  • On SFC Ryan Hendrickson, Afghanistan: “In 2010, Green Beret Ryan Hendrickson was leading his team through a Taliban-held village in Afghanistan at three in the morning when he… stepped on enemy explosives — a lot of them. The blast ripped through his lower body, and he looked down to see his shattered bones protruding from his absolutely mangled leg and arm. Certain that he would die, Ryan’s only thought as he was airlifted away was the men he was leaving behind… They told him his combat career was over, but Ryan was not done. Eighteen months later, he returned to Afghanistan… For his courage, he was awarded the Silver Star.” (Watch)
  • On Marine veteran Dale Garner, Beirut: “As a young man, Dale Garner enlisted in the Marines after the Iran Hostage Crisis. Soon, he deployed to Beirut on a mission of peace — but on the morning of October 23, 1983, Iranian-backed Hezbollah terrorists… detonated a truck packed with explosives at the Marine barracks with hundreds of Americans inside… He was the sole survivor of the men around him, and he joins us here to remember the 241 American service members murdered in the Beirut barracks bombing, the deadliest day for the Marine Corps since Iwo Jima.” (Watch)

From the day he returned to the White House, President Trump has placed America’s veterans at the center of his agenda:

  • Lower drug costs: Prescription drug prices have posted their sharpest drop in more than 60 years, and the VA has secured more than $10 billion in pharmaceutical savings this fiscal year alone.
  • Faster benefits: President Trump signed an Executive Order modernizing data sharing between the Departments of War and Veterans Affairs to speed veterans’ access to benefits and employment opportunities.
  • Mental health breakthroughs: President Trump signed an Executive Order to accelerate access to treatments for serious mental illness — especially for our veterans, who suffer higher rates of serious mental illness and suicide.
  • New careers: President Trump launched Freedom Haulers, a Department of Transportation fast-track program to help service members earn their Commercial Driver’s License.
  • Relief for veterans on fixed incomes: The Working Families Tax Cuts delivered historic tax relief on Social Security for seniors and an unprecedented $50 billion investment to transform rural healthcare.
  • CHAMPVA backlog eliminated: In November 2025, the Trump Administration wiped out the entire CHAMPVA backlog — more than 70,000 unprocessed applications inherited from the Biden Administration.
  • A home for homeless veterans: President Trump signed an Executive Order to improve veterans’ care and accountability, expand options to cut wait times, and establish the National Center for Warrior Independence to house up to 6,000 homeless veterans by 2028.
  • A first-term promise kept: In his first term, he signed an Executive Order ensuring veterans have seamless access to mental health care and suicide prevention resources as they return to civilian life, especially in the critical first year.

Under President Trump’s leadership, the Department of Veterans Affairs is delivering for those who served:

  • Housing heroes: More than 95,000 homeless veterans housed in FY2025 and FY2026 — the two highest years on record.
  • Slashing the backlog: The benefits backlog is down nearly 70% since January 20, 2025, and average disability claims processing time is down 46%.
  • Record claims: A record 3.11 million compensation claims processed in FY2026 — up 23.5% from FY2024 — with nearly 94% accuracy.
  • More veterans in care: More than 330,000 new veterans enrolled in VA health care in 2026, and record highs of 82.7 million direct care and 68.1 million community care appointments in FY2026.
  • Care on veterans’ schedules: More than 3.5 million early-morning, evening, and weekend appointments offered since January 20, 2025.
  • Modern facilities: Opened 47 new health care clinics and invested nearly $5 billion in FY2026 to modernize and repair VA facilities — the largest maintenance investment in VA history.
  • Health records back on track: VA’s electronic health record modernization is back on track, now deployed at new sites in Ohio, Kentucky, Michigan, Indiana, and Alaska.
  • Protecting veterans’ homes: Reformed VA home loan protections to keep veterans from losing their homes to foreclosure.

This morning, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth systematically dismantled the desperate, ego-driven impeachment hoax by a disgruntled and defeated Congressman. Secretary Hegseth made clear that every operation targeted in the eight articles was lawful, ordered by the Commander-in-Chief, properly notified to Congress, and carried out by warriors who delivered decisive results. He also made clear that this is not oversight; it is a political spectacle aimed at President Donald J. Trump and the men and women who defend our country.

  • “What one disgruntled and defeated Congressman is attempting is not oversight and it’s not accountability. It’s a political spectacle — a personal manifesto driven by ego and resentment, timed for one man’s final days in Congress to try to do damage to this President, this country, and most irresponsibly, the Warriors who defend it. It’s a farce and it’s a stunt, and everybody knows it.” (Watch)
  • “In the 250 years of our American Republic, no Secretary of War or Secretary of Defense has ever been impeached for carrying out lawful military operations — and in our case, successful ones at that — not once, War Powers resolution or not. Not under Reagan in Lebanon; not under Clinton in Kosovo; not under Obama in Iraq and Syria; not under Biden in Iraq and Syria. That’s the standard… And one disgruntled Congressman wants to shred it over policy disagreements.” (Watch)
  • “That’s what it is: policy disagreements — not high crimes, not misdemeanors, not treason, not bribery, not the kinds of offenses the founders intended when they wrote the impeachment clause. The proper remedy for a policy disagreement? It’s legislation. It’s debate. It’s the next Presidential election. It’s not handing the House and Senate floor to the Democrats so that they can run a show trial against the President and the Secretary of War while Republicans still control Congress and should be delivering wins for the American people.” (Watch)
  • “For the first time in American history, a Cabinet secretary overseeing America’s military is being attacked not for losing conflicts with our enemies, but for winning them. Condemned not for defeat, but for military victory.” (Watch)
  • “As for the articles themselves — Iran, the cartels, Maduro, Yemen — every one was a lawful operation ordered by the Commander-in-Chief, then ordered by myself, notified to Congress, and executed by American warriors who did their jobs.” (Watch)
  • “This is not about me. Politicians in Washington have accused the sailors and the pilots who struck narcoterrorist boats of war crimes for doing their job. Senators, in cute videos, have suggested the same. This resolution is the next step: put the Secretary on trial today and the men and women who carried out those orders tomorrow. If they want to come for the warriors, they’re going to have to come through me.” (Watch)
  • “We’ve seen this show before. They impeached President Trump over a perfect phone call; they impeached him again in his final week in office. Both times they failed, both times he came back stronger, and the American people sent him back to the White House. Now, they’re trying a third time — this time against a member of his Cabinet. They will fail again.” (Watch)
  • “Let’s be clear about what this resolution actually does. It tells our enemies — Iran, the cartels, every adversary watching — that the United States will actually punish its own warriors and its own civilian leadership for successfully executing lawful military operations… It puts a target on the backs of American warriors by signaling that Congress will undermine their missions in real time. This is not patriotism; this is sabotage.” (Watch)
  • “In Operation Epic Fury, by every measure, we achieved a historic military victory… We control the Strait of Hormuz. Crazy Islamists in Tehran will never, ever have a nuclear weapon. A historic effort, only made possible by a courageous Commander-in-Chief.” (Watch)
  • “From Day One, President Trump made homeland security national security. We sent American troops to lock down the southwest border and choked off the cartel pipeline of human smuggling, of drugs, and death. Then, we took the fight to them… Thousands of American lives saved with every drug boat sunk and every shipment prevented.” (Watch)
  • “President Trump gave this Department what it has not had in a generation: a Commander-in-Chief with the courage to lead and the resolve to win. I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them — and I would do it again tomorrow.” (Watch)
  • “We will not apologize for putting American lives first. We will not apologize for stopping the flow of drugs that kill our citizens. We will not apologize for destroying the capabilities of a regime that chants ‘death to America.’” (Watch)
  • “We’ve never had a better Commander-in-Chief, full stop. I get to watch him every single day. He lives and breathes America First and it’s the honor of a lifetime to be his Secretary of War.” (Watch)

The support for Secretary Hegseth has been swift and unambiguous:

President Donald J. Trump: “Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defense against a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman, Thomas Massie, a TOTAL LOSER!”

Vice President JD Vance: “Has Pete Hegseth committed impeachable crimes? The question is absurd and the answer is: obviously not. Like so much of Congress, impeachment has become a ridiculous show that stands in for actual policymaking. Congress has so many tools for registering its policy disagreements. Rather than use them, they’re going to try to impeach Pete Hegseth. They did the same to Donald Trump. Legislation is hard. Impeachments are easy (and ultimately, inconsequential). The irony is that legislators are most angry at Pete on the issues where he’s most correct: repositioning forces away from Europe/Ukraine and reorganizing the general officer corps. This isn’t about Iran, this is about the fact that Pete took on the bureaucracy at the Pentagon.”

Speaker of the House of Representatives Mike Johnson: “The impeachment effort is a political gambit for attention… The idea that you would impeach the Secretary of War at a time of international conflict sends a terrible message to our enemies and our allies, and we’re not going to play that game… It’s just purely for people to get attention, and it’s shameful.”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio: “Not only did Pete execute on a direct order from the Commander-in-Chief [who], in our Constitution, is empowered and trusted with the job of keeping Americans safe, but they did it quite effectively…”

Attorney General Todd Blanche: “He is executing on President Trump’s mission… When you hear [this] rhetoric coming out of the Hill that he’s doing something illegal or wrong, that’s not true — and guess what? Every single Congressman knows that… We very much support Pete and we very much support the work that he’s doing working for this Administration.”

Secretary of Veterans Affairs Doug Collins: “@SecWar has defended vital U.S. interests and helped inspire record-high recruiting levels in America’s Armed Forces. He’s also been a great partner as @DeptofWar and @DeptVetAffairs work together to support servicemembers as they transition to Veterans. Proud to call him a colleague and friend.”

Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum: “Together with @POTUS, @SecWar has overseen historically successful military operations, for which America, and the entire world, are safer. He has cut red tape to unleash innovation and modernize our military technologies. He has sent thousands of troops to secure the Southern Border. He has deployed the National Guard to make our cities, including our capital, safe again. And he has strengthened relationships with our allies to deter adversaries and protect the United States. This is America-First leadership in action.”

Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins: “Secretary Hegseth is doing exactly what President Trump promised for the American people: putting AMERICA FIRST and Making our Military STRONG Again. Our brave men and women in uniform deserve LEADERSHIP focused on defending our nation, not being dragged into political games. Alongside @SecWar: We will stand. We will fight. We will defend this republic.”

Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin: “Under the historic leadership of President Trump, @DHSgov has had NO stronger partner on border security than @PeteHegseth and @DeptofWar. Together, we have locked down the border, choked off the cartels’ pipeline, and saved American lives. Pete is a patriot and a warfighter, and I am proud to call him a friend.”

Secretary of Housing and Urban Development Scott Turner: “Under @SecWar’s leadership, our military has eliminated top threats to our homeland and modernized our warfighting capabilities to protect the American people. Impeaching the Secretary of War for lawful military action sets a dangerous precedent. Congress should be focused on representing and delivering real results for the American people.”

Administrator of the Small Business Administration Kelly Loeffler: “Thanks to @SecWar, military recruitment has reached record highs, the U.S. has eliminated dangerous terrorists and cartel leaders around the world, our border is secure, and our warfighters are stronger than ever – that’s what @POTUS promised his Admin would deliver. Secretary Hegseth has also already strengthened our supply chains by recognizing that small businesses comprise over 70% of the defense industrial base and are essential to American military readiness. It is my honor to work with him on our Smaller War Plants Commission, which is making historic investments in small manufacturers to bolster our capabilities, advance innovation, and grow the Arsenal of Freedom that secures peace through strength. I’m proud to stand with @SecWar and this vital mission.”

Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency Lee Zeldin: “Pete Hegseth is an American patriot and an exceptional Secretary of War! Military recruitment has been hitting record numbers and troop morale has been surging with @PeteHegseth at the tip of the spear.”

Sen. Bernie Moreno: “The idea that a failed Congressman wants to make a political point just because he’s bitter about a defeat is gross.”

Rep. Andrew Clyde: “As a 28-year Navy combat veteran, I know what it takes to protect our nation and preserve our freedoms. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has my full support.”

Rep. Randy Fine: “I trusted Pete Hegseth with my oldest son this summer when he joined the @USNavy. I don’t regret that decision one bit. Thomas Massie’s almost illiterate motion is a fitting disgrace for a petulant loser. Or what I’d expect from someone with the mental capacity of a pinecone. I stand with @SecWar.”

Rep. Nancy Mace: “Vote on Hegseth impeachment is at 5:30pm today – I will not be voting to impeach. The Iran war is through no fault of his own and he should not be the one scapegoated for it. I fully support the changes Hegseth has made to the DoW to make our fighting force the very best it can be.”

Rep. Cory Mills: “I will be supporting our @SecWar as he’s done an amazing job returning our military to its full strength and living the warrior ethos!”

Rep. Ralph Norman: “@SecWar has my full support, and I remain opposed to efforts to impeach him. He has worked tirelessly to restore strength at the Department of War by putting military readiness and our warfighters FIRST. No one has done more to reestablish the strength and credibility of our military on the world stage.”

Rep. Andy Ogles: “I stand with @SecWar… He’s a patriot who has delivered great results for our armed forces.”

Rep. Burgess Owens: “And for years we actually thought Massie was a ‘principled’ Republican… in the end, truth prevails. He’s always been a slick Democrat. Now an unhinged, angry one.”

Rep. William Timmons: “I stand firmly with Secretary Hegseth. Impeachment is one of the most serious powers entrusted to Congress, and Massie’s rush to bring these charges directly to the House floor treats that responsibility like a political stunt.”

Rep. Derrick Van Orden: “Massie is a shameless contrarian who is begging for attention by trying to impeach @secwar before he loses the platform he had as a member of congress. In FOURTEEN YEARS he has never got a bill signed into law. So what the hell has he been doing? Show Boating.”

Rep. Ryan Zinke: “I think it’s a classic case of showboating by a largely discredited, defeated, and disgraced lawmaker—Thomas Massie… I think Pete Hegseth has done a great job. This is unfortunate showboating from Thomas Massie.”

The Wall Street Journal Editorial Board: “Mr. Jeffries may think this is a free vote he can give his left-wingers before Democrats take control in January. But voters will see through this and notice that Democrats are more preoccupied with shooting at Mr. Hegseth than bringing the war in Iran to a victorious end.”

Macdonald-Laurier Institute Senior Fellow Brian L. Cox: “Hey Rep Massie. International law prof & retired military lawyer here. I read the articles of impeachment you filed against @SecWar today. And it’s clear you don’t have a clue what you’re talking about… Each of the articles includes an assertion that SECWAR Hegseth ‘will remain a threat to the Constitution if allowed to remain in office,’ or words to that effect. In reality, the articles of impeachment are a sham – from beginning to end. And it is Rep Massie, not Sec Hegseth, who IS a clear & present threat to the Constitution – for abusing the impeachment powers vested in Congress by distorting international AND domestic law to create the false appearance that Hegseth’s conduct amounts to ‘high Crimes and Misdemeanors.’”

Former White House Chief of Staff Reince Priebus: “What order did Pete Hegseth order or not follow-through on that is impeachable? Massie is a grandstanding axe grinder. This is all for show… There’s nothing here.”

Former Department of Justice Chief of Staff Chad Mizelle: “The War Powers Resolution of 1973 never names the Secretary of War or imposes any duties on him. Charging Hegseth with violating it for executing the President’s orders is a farce and a waste of time. Congress could be doing real work right now instead of staging a political spectacle over a statute that does not even apply to the person they are targeting.”

Fox News Channel Legal Editor Kerri Urbahn: “These Articles of Impeachment, particularly the ones saying that Secretary Hegseth violated the federal statute that talks about notifying Congress and the like, I think they just fall so short.”

The Washington Examiner Chief Political Correspondent Byron York: “Reading through Thomas Massie’s articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth. There are 8 articles. Articles 1, 2, and 3 all accuse Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution by waging war in Iran. You might ask yourself: Did Pete Hegseth order US forces into action in Iran? I thought President Trump did that. That’s a good question; from the very beginning, Hegseth appears to serve as a stand-in for Massie’s real desire, which is to impeach Trump… Massie is clearly pushing these articles because he is racing the clock against his own departure from Congress on January 3, having been defeated in a Republican primary in his home state of Kentucky. There is only so much time left to do damage, and with this BS impeachment, Massie is trying to make the most of it.”

Nassau County (NY) Executive Bruce Blakeman: “On the anniversary of the Marine Corps I find it disgraceful that Thomas Massie would move to impeach Pete Hegseth a military veteran and Patriot who restored our military capabilities. Massie is a petulant and small man not worthy of serving in the House of Representatives.”

Veteran Action Founder Mark Lucas: “Side with Massie and Jeffries to impeach Pete Hegseth, and you won’t have a future in the Republican Party. @VeteranAction is watching every vote. Vote NO.”

Veteran Action: “Thomas Massie is a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman. Veteran Action stands with @PeteHegseth. Tell Congress to vote NO on the impeachment.”

Article III Project Founder and President Mike Davis: “This Hegseth impeachment is garbage. Congress declares war. The president makes war. He can repel sudden attack. He can protect American troops, assets, and allies. He does not need a declaration of war. Where were Massie’s articles of impeachment against Lloyd Austin after Afghanistan? They won’t go after Trump. So they go after Pete. Pete Hegseth is a bold and fearless warrior for the Constitution. He is highly effective. He is doing his job. Call your House Rep. Oppose this bogus impeachment.”

Former Deputy National Security Adviser Victoria Coates: “It’s political theater at its worst because the subject is deadly serious. These are our warfighters and they’re being used as pawns. Unfortunately, I think this is a preview of what we’re going to see out of the next Democrat Congress. Congressman Massie should be ashamed of himself for trying to take advantage of these last couple of weeks for this kind of performance.”

NewsNation host Katie Pavlich: “After months of claiming they care about affordability, Democrats in Congress, along with Republican losers like Thomas Massie and Thom Tillis, have their sights focused on Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. They’re demanding impeachment, citing an array of emotional reasons and international law that doesn’t exist… Hegseth is a patriot fulfilling his oath.”

Harvard Law Professor Emeritus Alan Dershowitz: “I would be honored to help defend him because these are not impeachable offenses… None of the grounds that are in the Massie allegations come even close to meeting that standard.”

Attorney Mehek Cooke: “As an attorney my advice to @RepThomasMassie: @SecWar isn’t going anywhere. YOU are. SCOTUS rejected Congress bypassing the President to issue binding orders. You can’t impeach Hegseth for defying an order Congress lacked power to issue. Your articles lack legal foundation.”

Article III Project Senior Counsel Will Chamberlain: “Everything about this Hegseth impeachment is like a perfect microcosm of @RepThomasMassie’s passive-aggressiveness, cowardice, resentment, and envy.
– He’s trying to get Hegseth impeached instead of Trump, who he’s still too cowardly to go after personally.
– He’s going after Hegseth because Hegseth endorsed against him in his primary.
– He’s using legal arguments he knows are frivolous. Thomas Massie has been in the House for well over a decade, he knows concurrent resolutions are non-binding, but he’s saying that failing to defy his commander-in-chief and adhere to a non-binding Congressional resolution is an impeachable offense.
– And to top it all off, he’s saying ‘this is all for Hegseth’s own good’ with a smug insinuation that the evidence Massie does not possess will doom him.
– This, from the guy who talked about ‘how much work he and Trump still had to do together’ during his primary, and who published an out-of-date Trump endorsement when Trump had endorsed his opponent.
Thomas Massie is a weak, pathetic excuse for a man.”

Journalist Lara Logan: “The Sec of War has not committed any crime. Massie cannot possibly be so ignorant to the functioning of govt that he does not know the principal military advisors to the President on war in Iran are the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs & the Centcom Commander. So if the Iran war is his issue, he is going after the wrong man. Punishing Pete Hegseth for restoring the U.S. Military to the strength & organization needed to defend this country from all enemies both foreign & domestic is an odd choice. I relish all the attacks that will come at me for saying this – bring it on. Massie is wrong.”

Samaritan’s Purse President Franklin Graham: “I believe the real reason they are coming after Secretary Hegseth is because he has taken on the anti-God, woke, and DEI initiatives that the Biden administration had pushed down the throats of our military. Since Secretary Hegseth has been at the Pentagon, he’s been cleaning house—and millions of Americans are grateful. I encourage everyone to pray for him, that God would give him strength for this difficult hour.”

Article III Project Senior Counsel Josh Hammer: “Patriots stand with @PeteHegseth.”

Lieutenant Colonel Robert “Buzz” Patterson, USAF (Ret.): “Massie is trying to impeach him and @PeteHegseth is changing our military for the better! This is huge! I support Pete. He’s a great dude and we need him.”

Center for Renewing America Executive Director Wade Miller: “The good news is that voters already impeached Massie. He was one of the biggest facilitators of big spending in DC all while he fakely postured on it to Americans. His entire sham impeachment effort is merely revenge because Trump endorsed against him. Weaponizing impeachments like this is exceedingly corrupt and Congress will now be less corrupt once Massie is out of office.”

The Dossier Publisher Jordan Schachtel: “Would be beyond absurd for any GOP rep to vote for impeachment. SecWar has done a terrific job revitalizing the military and has served his country admirably.”

Advancing American Freedom Senior Legal Fellow Hans von Spakovsky: “Massie is abusing impeachment power; it’s not intended to be used as political weapon when you disagree with policy but only for serious misconduct”

Article III Project: “Rep. Thomas Massie filed an impeachment resolution against Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, and Democrats are itching to run with it. The House must kill it. Hegseth committed no treason. He took no bribe. No evidence shows corruption or any other crime.”

California Post Opinion Editor Joel Pollak: “Impeachment of a cabinet member for doing his job, even badly (not the case here), is unconstitutional. It’s why I opposed the impeachment of the (truly awful) Mayorkas under Biden. Media cheerleaders remind us they are siding with one party — and with America’s enemy in wartime.”

Commentator Glenn Beck: “Pete Hegseth is everything the DC establishment hates, and that’s why they’re making him a scapegoat. He transformed the Department of War from a gay, woke, weak cesspool into a deadly fighting force once again. He has inspired our warriors to serve their country, not their ideology. He has made it clear to our enemies that the United States military will not be mocked. That is his real ‘crime’ against the establishment that was managing America’s decline. They’re trying to make this all about the Iran War. But that’s Trump’s conflict. If you think it’s an illegal war, your argument is with the man we elected as Commander-in-Chief, not the man he chose to run the department.”

Commentator Mark Levin: “Seeking the impeachment of the Secretary of War in the middle of military operations against the Iranian regime, without a single legitimate impeachable allegation, is among the evilest and most diabolical acts of any political majority/party in our history! The entire Democrat Party and a freak Republican on his way out of Congress giving aid and comfort to the enemy– an enemy that has killed and maimed thousands of Americans, sought the assassination of the president and others, and will get nuclear weapons if it is not defeated. History will remember this, depending on how long this republic survives.”

America First Policy Institute: “Under @SECWAR’s leadership, the U.S. military hit a 15-YEAR recruiting high across all 5 branches. Americans are PROUD to wear the uniform and serve our great Nation.”

Tea Party Patriots Co-Founder Jenny Beth Martin: “Hegseth just laid it out. This impeachment push tells Iran and every adversary that we will punish our own warriors for winning a lawful fight. One rogue legislator with a personal grudge does not get to veto the commander in chief. This is not patriotism. This is sabotage.”

Tea Party Patriots: “The House votes at 5:30 tonight on impeaching Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. Thomas Massie, who lost his primary for re-election, forced the vote. ‘None of these are high crimes or misdemeanors.’ Pete Hegseth is right.”

Last night, President Donald J. Trump sat down with 60 Minutes following the midterm elections and made a powerful case for his America First record. President Trump highlighted the booming Trump economy — 165,000 new jobs in October, record 401(k) balances, and hundreds of billions of dollars in new factories — touted the most secure border in history, detailed the decisive blows he has dealt to Iran’s nuclear program, explained why America must win the Super Intelligence race, and much more.

Key exchanges:

  • On the midterms: “I think if I was on the ballot, it would’ve been a much different situation… But there’s something beyond that. They didn’t like the war. They didn’t like the fact that gasoline went up… And there’s a great dislike, incredibly, for Israel.” (Watch)
  • On the stock market: “We have historically good numbers. We have the highest stock market in history.” (Watch)
    • Since President Trump was elected, the S&P 500 has hit 77 new record highs, the Nasdaq has hit 70 record highs, and the Dow has hit 51 record highs. Since Inauguration Day, the S&P 500 has hit 67 record highs, the Nasdaq has hit 60 record highs, and the Dow has hit 43 record highs.
  • On jobs numbers: “The numbers are way beyond anybody’s expectations… We had 165,000 jobs created just in a short time.” (Watch)
    • The U.S. economy added 165,000 new jobs in October — smashing economists’ expectations; manufacturing added 19,000 jobs in October and the sector has added more than 100,000 jobs since its December 2025 low.
  • On retirement savings: “401(k)s are at their all-time high by a lot. Under other Presidents, they were a disaster. 401(k)s have made people rich.”  (Watch)
    • 401(k), 403(b), and IRA balances hit new highs in the second quarter of 2026, with the average 401(k) balance reaching a record $155,800 — up 13.1% from a year earlier.
  • On private investment: “There has never been a time where there is the activity — trillions and trillions of dollars right now, as we sit, is being built. In a year from now… many of those plants are gonna be open, operating.” (Watch)
    • Companies are pouring money into America, including Apple ($600 billion and 20,000 new American hires), NVIDIA (up to $500 billion in American-made SI infrastructure), TSMC ($165 billion in the largest single foreign direct investment in U.S. history), and Johnson & Johnson (more than $55 billion).
  • On reshoring auto manufacturing: “We’re also building automobile factories like we’ve never built before.” (Watch)
    • Audi is building its first-ever U.S. plant in Georgia, with a $4 billion investment that will create about 4,500 new jobs.
  • On reshoring pharmaceutical manufacturing: “How about pharmaceutical? Eli Lilly, Merck, Pfizer — they’re building hundreds of billions of [investment].” (Watch)
    • Eli Lilly has committed more than $50 billion to American manufacturing, Merck has committed more than $70 billion, and Pfizer has committed an additional $70 billion as part of its landmark agreement with the Trump Administration to lower drug prices.
  • On securing the border: “I think I got an A+ for closing up the border… I get very high marks for getting the bad ones out.” (Watch)
    • Border Patrol recorded just 98,708 southwest border apprehensions in FY2026 — the lowest in agency history and a 95% drop from the Biden-era average — while September marked the 17th straight month of zero releases at the border.
  • On Iran: “You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon. I think, historically, this will be a very good decision. Is it a good decision for today and tomorrow? Maybe not, but I have to go with what’s right for our country.” (Watch)
  • On the Strait of Hormuz: “The strait is open, Ross… Your favorite newspaper, The Wall Street Journal… had an article that said, ‘There’s more oil going through the Hormuz Strait than there was at the beginning of the war.’ Think of that.” (Watch)
    • The Wall Street Journal reports that Persian Gulf oil exports have surpassed prewar levels — more than 24 million barrels a day — thanks to a shipping system under U.S. protection.
  • On Venezuela: “I just say the Venezuela attack will go down in military histories… It was one of the most incredible attacks anyone’s ever seen. They left the aircraft carriers at 1:00 in the morning, pitch black. Everything went perfect.” (Watch)
  • On the Russia-Ukraine war: “I believe that war is going to end and it’s going to end soon, and the only reason it’s going to end is because of me.” (Watch)
  • On Super Intelligence: “The reason I’m an AI bull, one of the reasons, is because President Xi left here two weeks ago — we had a great meeting — he’s all-in to SI… Whoever wins that race wins.” (Watch)
  • On data centers: “China has no problem with data centers. China has no problem with electricity. And, by the way, we don’t either because… I’m demanding that they build their own electric plant.” (Watch)
  • On MAGA: “MAGA is basically common sense. MAGA is strong borders, good military — we have created wealth at a level that our country has never seen before.” (Watch)
  • On 2028: “We have a tremendous bench.” (Watch)
  • On how his presidency will be remembered: “That I made America great again.” (Watch)

Today, President Donald J. Trump announced the appointment of Stephen Miller as the 33rd White House Chief of Staff, succeeding Susie Wiles after her highly successful tenure. Miller has served alongside President Trump since the very beginning and has been a driving force behind the Administration’s major successes — driving violent crime to historic lows, securing the border at unprecedented levels, and dismantling large-scale fraud. He brings deep experience, broad institutional knowledge, and unwavering commitment to the role.

The news was met with widespread praise:

Vice President JD Vance: “Very grateful to Susie for her friendship and service to the president and our country. Stephen Miller is an amazing patriot and will do great things. Congrats to him on a well deserved promotion!”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio: “Susie Wiles served our country with exceptional strength, devotion, and grace. She has done an incredible job serving our country and President Trump. I am grateful for her service, her friendship, and I wish her continued success in her next chapter. I look forward to continuing to work with Stephen Miller, one of the President’s most trusted and longtime advisors, to advance the President’s agenda.”

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth: “Huge CONGRATS to @StephenM — a true patriot and America First fighter. He never backs down — and the @DeptofWar is right there with him.”

Attorney General Todd Blanche: “A huge thank you to Susie Wiles for her incredible service to our nation! She’s a rockstar and will no doubt continue working to make our country great. Looking forward to continuing our work with my good friend Stephen Miller as Chief. Together we’ve reduced crime to historic levels, enhanced public safety throughout our communities, and continue to root out the massive fraud that has taken advantage of American taxpayers. We’re not slowing down.”

Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum: “@SusieWiles47 is a talented leader and tireless champion for the American people. Her relentless determination and unwavering commitment to our country have set an example for everyone in this administration. America is better because of her service, and I’m grateful to have had the opportunity to work alongside her. Looking forward to working with @StephenM in his new role as we continue the Golden Age of America!”

Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins: “Thank you, @SusieWiles47! From helping lead President Trump’s historic comeback to serving as the first woman White House Chief of Staff, you’ve led with kindness and resolve. It has been a privilege to serve alongside you and I will never forget those early 2021 days when only a few of us were in the arena. And speaking of just a few of us in the arena back then… Congratulations to @StephenM! You and Katie are true patriots. Excited to continue our work together on fraud, making school lunches healthy again, and bringing real prosperity back to rural America. No worthier causes than these and no better leader than you to make it so. There’s more work ahead to deliver @POTUS’ America First agenda, and we’re ready. Let’s get it done!”

Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling: “Congratulations to @StephenM on becoming @WhiteHouse Chief of Staff. I have had the privilege of working alongside Stephen during both Trump Administrations. I know firsthand the dedication, work ethic, and commitment that he will bring to the Chief of Staff position and I look forward to working with him to continue delivering on @POTUS’ agenda as he steps into his new role.”

Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.: “Next to me, Stephen Miller is the strongest MAHA supporter in the administration. It’s time to unleash the Kraken.”

Secretary of Housing and Urban Development Scott Turner: “@StephenM is a true patriot. Thanks to his partnership, President Trump put an end to government control of suburbs, improved housing affordability, and enhanced accountability in public benefit programs. He is fearless, focused, and ready to drive President Trump’s agenda for the American people. He will do a great job!”

Secretary of Energy Chris Wright: “Congratulations to @StephenM on his appointment as White House Chief of Staff. I’ve appreciated Stephen’s partnership and his unwavering commitment to delivering on President Trump’s vision for America. I look forward to continuing our work together. And a heartfelt thank you to @SusieWiles47 for her exceptional leadership, friendship, and service to our country.”

Secretary of Education Linda McMahon: “Congratulations to @StephenM! We’ve been in this fight together for a long time, and I look forward to continuing our work to Make America Great Again! A legacy of distinguished service as our nation’s first female White House Chief of Staff. Thank you, @SusieWiles47, for your extraordinary leadership!”

Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin: “Excited for my friend @StephenM. President Trump made an excellent choice by choosing him as his chief of staff. Under @SusieWiles47’s leadership, I personally learned a great deal from her on how she handled personal adversity and balanced a strong work ethic. It’s an honor to be in the fight with so many great America First patriots.”

Director of the Office of Management and Budget Russ Vought: “Congratulations to @StephenM who will do an incredible job for President Trump as the new Chief of Staff! He is a world class talent and deeply committed to the President and the America First agenda. He will do great!”

Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency Lee Zeldin: “Stephen Miller is an incredibly talented fighter who’s been by President Trump’s side from DAY ONE. He’s ready…always! Few are as sharp, loyal, and relentless in delivering for the President. A tried, true, and battle tested patriot.”

I look forward to working with @StephenM as our new White House Chief of Staff. Stephen has been a friend and colleague since the first Trump administration. I know his resolve and his commitment to this country, and I have no doubt he’ll bring both to leading this team for President Trump.”

Administrator of the Social Security Administration Frank Bisignano: “Congratulations @StephenM on being named WH Chief of Staff. I look forward to continuing our work together on behalf of American taxpayers, protecting the integrity of our programs at @SocialSecurity & @IRSnews. Thank you @SusieWiles47 for your historic service to our nation.”

Administrator of NASA Jared Isaacman: “Congrats to @StephenM, the new White House Chief of Staff”

President Donald J. Trump has long said that America is the hottest country in the world — and today’s blockbuster jobs report delivers the proof. The economy added a massive 165,000 new jobs in October, more than double what experts expected, with the unemployment rate falling, manufacturing surging, prior months revised sharply higher, and broad-based gains. Experts agree: this is a booming labor market.

Here’s what they’re saying:

Edward Jones Senior Global Strategist Angelo Kourkafas: “This was a blowout jobs report. Payroll growth exceeded expectations, revisions were positive, the unemployment rate fell, participation improved, and wage growth strengthened.”

EY-Parthenon Chief Economist Gregory Daco: “It’s as good as can be, really.”

Allianz Trade North America Senior Economist Dan North: “You have to look pretty hard to find something to dislike in there. It’s a really, really good report, and all around I think you’d say it’s stronger than expected and the best one in a while, and it kind of fits with what I call the stable but perhaps unexciting labor market.”

Edward Jones Head of Investment Strategy Mona Mahajan: “This is a strong number. It supports the view that the underlying fundamentals of this economy have held in there. We’ve seen a strong manufacturing economy, we’ve seen a strong services economy, and we see a pretty robust labor market.”

Principal Asset Management Chief Global Strategist Seema Shah: “Today’s jobs report is a strong rebuttal to fears that the economy is heading into a meaningful slowdown. Payrolls growth surprised firmly to the upside, unemployment fell back to 4.1%, and job creation remains broad-based, pointing to an economy that is still absorbing labor comfortably rather than one beginning to buckle under tighter financial conditions.”

Fitch Ratings Head of U.S. Economics Olu Sonola: “Strength on strength. This is a very strong labor-market report on the heels of solid GDP and consumer-spending data last week, reinforcing the economy’s positive momentum.”

Bloomberg Senior Editor Chris Anstey: “It’s worth noting that, with the October gain in factory payrolls, total manufacturing employment is now a net positive since Trump returned to office.”

Prescription drug prices are plummeting for the first time in decades under the leadership of President Donald J. Trump — delivering real, measurable relief to millions of Americans. In City Journal, Dr. Joel Zinberg explains why this is a major accomplishment:

“Yet few Americans realize that drug prices—a major complaint—are actually falling.

The Consumer Price Index for prescription drugs has either fallen or been flat every month of 2026. The latest inflation data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics show that while the overall CPI rose 3.7 percent year to year, prescription drug prices fell 4.5 percent—the largest year-over-year decline since 1963—and nonprescription prices fell 0.9 percent…

The Trump administration has pursued multiple policies to bring drug prices down. TrumpRx, launched in February 2026, provides cash-paying patients with large discounts on over 800 drugs, including many of the most popular medicines. Chief among these are the GLP-1 weight-loss drugs. U.S. prescription drug spending surged in 2025, driven by increased utilization of the GLP-1s tirzepatide and semaglutide at approximately $60 billion each. Consumers’ use of the TrumpRx discounts—particularly for GLP-1s—has been a major factor in lowering prescription prices throughout 2026.

Agreements with pharmaceutical companies Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk reduce the cost of GLP-1 medications for government programs and TrumpRx while expanding Medicare coverage for obesity with a $50 monthly copay. TrumpRx prices are most valuable to uninsured patients and those whose private plans do not cover GLP-1s to treat obesity. (Less than a third of employer-provided health plans cover GLP-1s for obesity.) By providing low, transparent prices to consumers, these programs create downward pressure on drug prices in all insurance plans.”

American manufacturing is surging under President Donald J. Trump. A new report shows the sector expanding for the tenth consecutive month, with production growing at its fastest pace in nearly five years. Factories are expanding. Jobs are returning. Paychecks are rising faster than inflation. And companies are investing trillions to build their futures in America.

  • Manufacturing jobs are coming back. Manufacturers have added 72,000 jobs this year, reversing the 202,000 manufacturing jobs lost in the final two years of the Biden Administration. Employment in factory construction has climbed by nearly 112,000 since President Trump took office.
  • Paychecks are growing. Manufacturing workers’ weekly earnings are up 5% over the past year — outpacing inflation and boosting purchasing power.
  • Investment is accelerating. Business investment jumped 12.7% in the third quarter of 2026, the fastest growth in 15 years. Private investment in plants and equipment rose 9.4% — more than twice the 2025 rate and triple the pace of Biden’s final year. Capital goods imports hit a record share of total goods imports in September while consumer goods imports fell to a historic low, signaling businesses are equipping American factories, not just importing finished products.
  • Demand for American machinery is strong. U.S. machine tool orders reached their third-highest monthly total on record, up more than 36% from a year earlier.

Companies are matching the momentum with major new commitments. In just the past few weeks:

  • Audi announced a $4 billion factory in Georgia — its first U.S. manufacturing plant — creating 4,500 jobs.
  • Westinghouse Electric announced a $1 billion investment in South Carolina to build a next-generation nuclear fuel factory.
  • U.S. Steel announced a $3 billion investment near Pittsburgh to construct a new hot strip mill and increase annual capacity by roughly 1.3 million tons.
  • Apple announced up to $100 million to strengthen American titanium production.
  • Bombardier announced $270 million in U.S. manufacturing investment, creating thousands of jobs.
  • Carrier announced more than $600 million in an advanced manufacturing facility in Fort Worth.

More jobs. Rising wages. New factories. Record investment. Under President Trump, American manufacturing is being rebuilt — and made great again.

President Donald J. Trump has executed the most sweeping restoration of American sovereignty, strength, and prosperity in modern history. With ferocious speed and resolve, President Trump has reversed decades of decline, kept more promises than any modern President, and delivered results for working families that once seemed impossible.

Here are 127 Promises Made, Promises Kept from President Trump’s second term:

Ending the Border Invasion and Restoring American Sovereignty

  • PROMISE MADE: “We will close the border. We will stop the invasion of illegals into our country.” (10/12/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: Under President Trump, illegal crossings at the southern border have collapsed to the lowest levels in American history after his rapid action to close the border on Day One. In FY 2026, Border Patrol recorded just 98,708 southwest border apprehensions — a 95% drop from the more than 1.8 million per year under Biden — and nationwide encounters fell to the lowest in the agency’s history.

  • PROMISE MADE: “I will send troops to the southern border to repel the disastrous invasion of our country.” (1/20/25)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: On Day One, President Trump declared a national emergency at the southern border and deployed thousands of military personnel to protect it — establishing National Defense Areas where illegal crossers can be charged with trespassing on a military installation.

  • PROMISE MADE: “I will immediately end the Biden border nightmare that traffickers are using to exploit vulnerable women and children.” (7/21/23)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: The number of unaccompanied illegal migrant children crossing into the country remains near a record-low, with Customs and Border Protection encountering just 763 unaccompanied minors at the southern border in August 2026 — down nearly 95% from the 14,237 encountered in August 2023 under Biden.

  • PROMISE MADE: “325,000 children are missing or dead. They came through the border… 325,000 children went through her stupid open border, and now they’re either missing, dead, or slaves. If you want to end this disaster, you must get out and vote.” (11/1/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: After the Biden Administration lost track of 325,000 migrant children, the Trump Administration has located over 157,000 — fulfilling President Trump’s promise to do everything possible to save child victims of human trafficking.

  • PROMISE MADE: “Under my leadership, we will seal it up and expand that wall until we have total control.” (3/4/23)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump immediately resumed construction of the border wall, securing a historic $46.5 billion to build it as part of the Working Families Tax Cuts. CBP has completed 250 miles of new border barrier since January 20, 2025, and has obligated $34.3 billion to Smart Wall projects since September 2025.

  • PROMISE MADE: “I will end catch-and-release.” (10/12/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump ended catch-and-release on Day One. FY2026 was the first fiscal year in American history with zero Border Patrol releases, and the Trump Administration has not released a single illegal alien from the border into the U.S. interior for 17 straight months.

  • PROMISE MADE: “We will reinstate my Remain in Mexico policy.” (1/20/25)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: Soon after taking office, President Trump reinstated the “Remain in Mexico” policy — ensuring would-be illegal border crossers are not able to wait with little consequence in the U.S. for the resolution of their cases.

  • PROMISE MADE: “To further deter illegal immigration, I will sign on Day One [an] Executive Order ending automatic citizenship for the children of illegal aliens.” (7/1/23)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump immediately signed an Executive Order ending birthright citizenship for the children of illegal immigrants.

  • PROMISE MADE: “Kamala’s app for illegals will be shut down immediately — within 24 hours.” (10/12/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump ended the app’s use almost immediately after taking office and repurposed it as a mechanism for self-deportation.

  • PROMISE MADE: “I will… suspend refugee admissions, stop the resettlement, and keep the terrorists the hell out of our country.” (7/27/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump suspended refugee resettlement on Day One and slashed refugee admissions by more than 80%. He terminated Temporary Protected Status for 13 countries, including Somalia, Venezuela, and Haiti, and reduced the number of so-called “asylum seekers” entering the U.S. through ports of entry by a staggering 99.9%.

  • PROMISE MADE: “On Day One, I will immediately restore and expand the Trump travel ban.” (10/23/23)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump restored the travel ban in June 2025 and expanded it in December, imposing full entry restrictions on nationals of 19 high-risk countries.

Launching the Largest Deportation Operation in American History

  • PROMISE MADE: “We will begin the largest deportation operation in the history of our country.” (10/21/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: The illegal alien population has been reduced by at least 2.3 million, with more than three million illegal aliens leaving the country — including nearly 1.2 million who have been deported or removed. ICE has carried out nearly 1.3 million arrests, more than doubled its ranks of officers and agents, and secured more than 2,500 partnerships with state and local law enforcement, and President Trump signed the Secure America Act to deliver $70 billion more for ICE and CBP. In 2025, America recorded negative net migration for the first time in at least 50 years.

  • PROMISE MADE: “The drug cartels are waging war on America — and it’s now time for America to wage war on the cartels” (12/22/23); “We will expel every single illegal alien gang member and migrant criminal operating on American soil and remove the savage gang, Tren de Aragua, from the United States.” (1/19/25)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump designated more than ten Latin American cartels — including Tren de Aragua, MS-13, and Clan del Golfo — as terrorist organizations, invoked the Alien Enemies Act, and has arrested more than 12,100 gang members, including more than 1,500 Tren de Aragua and nearly 2,000 MS-13 affiliates. Through Operation Southern Spear, the U.S. military has struck more than 70 narco-terrorist vessels, and in Operation Absolute Resolve, U.S. forces captured indicted narco-terrorist dictator Nicolás Maduro and brought him to face justice in New York.

  • PROMISE MADE: “My administration will deliver justice for every family whose loved one has been stolen from them by migrant crime, including Laken Riley, Rachel Morin, Jocelyn Nungaray, Kayla Hamilton, and every other precious American soul that we have lost to these animals. Their memories will live in their hearts forever and our hearts forever, and we will never, ever forget them.” (1/19/25)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump signed the Laken Riley Act into law as his first legislative victory of his second term. The bill mandates the detention and deportation of illegal alien criminals and allows states to sue if immigration laws aren’t enforced.

  • PROMISE MADE: “I’m hereby calling for the death penalty for any migrant that kills an American citizen or a law enforcement officer.” (10/12/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump directed the Department of Justice to pursue the death penalty in capital crimes committed by illegal immigrants.

  • PROMISE MADE: “I am announcing a new plan to end all sanctuary cities in North Carolina and all across our country… and we will bring down the full weight of the federal government on any jurisdiction that refuses to cooperate.” (9/21/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: The Trump Administration has targeted so-called “sanctuary” jurisdictions giving safe harbor to criminal illegal immigrants — terminating sanctuary policies in Washington, D.C., and moving to strip federal funding from sanctuary jurisdictions nationwide.

Restoring Law and Order in American Communities

  • PROMISE MADE: “We will make America safe again.” (11/4/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: In 2025, the U.S. murder rate fell 18.1% — tying the lowest rate ever recorded — and violent crime posted the largest annual drop on record. In the first half of 2026, violent crime fell another 10.6% and murders dropped another 23%. Drug overdose deaths have fallen more than 40% from the Biden-era peak.
