  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: One week after taking office, President Trump signed an Executive Order restoring high standards for military readiness and ending woke gender ideology in the armed forces.

  • PROMISE MADE: “We did win two world wars from Fort Bragg… This is no time to be changing names… We’re going to do everything we can to get it back.” (10/4/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump restored the name Fort Bragg, and in June 2025, President Trump announced the restoration of the historic names of seven more Army bases, including Fort Hood, Fort Gordon, Fort Polk, and Fort A.P. Hill.

  • PROMISE MADE: “We got to take care of our veterans here. They’re among our greatest people… I will put veterans first and America first every single time.” (11/11/23)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: Under President Trump, the VA has cut the disability claims backlog by more than 70% and processed more veterans’ claims in FY 2026 than in any year in its history, delivering benefits faster to the heroes who defended our great nation. President Trump also approved a tax-free $1,776 Warrior Dividend for each of our nation’s 1.5 million active-duty service members.

Ending Government Weaponization and Restoring Equal Justice

  • PROMISE MADE: “Biden has worked to persecute political dissidents, including conservatives, Catholics and other Christians, and opponents of his weaponized state… This abuse will be rectified, and it will be rectified very quickly.” (5/25/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump has purged corrupt elements from the DOJ and FBI, pardoned pro-life Americans wrongly targeted by the Biden Administration, and launched full-scale investigations into deep state abuses — bringing the era of weaponized government to an end and restoring fairness and trust in American institutions.

  • PROMISE MADE: “I will commute the sentence of Ross Ulbricht… He’s already served 11 years. We’re going to get him home.” (5/25/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump granted Ross Ulbricht — who had been sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole in 2015 — a full and unconditional pardon, going even further than a commutation. As President Trump said, “The scum that worked to convict him were some of the same lunatics who were involved in the modern-day weaponization of government against me.”

  • PROMISE MADE: “My first acts as your next President will be to Close the Border, DRILL, BABY, DRILL, and Free the January 6 Hostages being wrongfully imprisoned!” (3/11/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: On his first day back in office, President Trump pardoned Americans convicted of offenses related to January 6, 2021, commuted the sentences of 14 others, and directed the dismissal of pending indictments — ending the Biden Administration’s persecution of these Americans.

Protecting Social Security and Medicare

  • PROMISE MADE: “I will not cut one penny from Social Security or Medicare … I will not talk about one day or one year shorter, and I will not raise the retirement age of Social Security by one day, not by one year.” (7/27/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump hasn’t touched Social Security — and has repeatedly promised he never will as the Administration roots out waste, fraud, and abuse to safeguard the programs’ solvency. In fact, the Department of Justice, supporting the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, recently charged 17 individuals accused of stealing over $1.3 million in Social Security benefits.

Making America Healthy Again

  • PROMISE MADE: “I’m going to let him go wild on health. I’m going to let him go wild on the food. I’m going to let him go wild on medicines.” (10/27/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: With Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., leading the charge, the Trump Administration released new dietary guidelines that put whole, nutrient-dense food ahead of processed junk and secured historic pledges from major food manufacturers to strip artificial dyes out of the products Americans eat and drink. President Trump also signed the Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act, restoring nutritious milk to America’s schools.

  • PROMISE MADE: “HHS will play a big role in helping ensure that everybody will be protected from harmful chemicals, pollutants, pesticides, pharmaceutical products, and food additives that have contributed to the overwhelming Health Crisis in this Country.” (11/14/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump established the Make America Healthy Again Commission to end the childhood chronic disease crisis. The FDA is phasing out petroleum-based synthetic dyes from the nation’s food supply and has proposed closing the GRAS loophole by requiring manufacturers to notify the agency when they conclude an ingredient added to food is safe. 23 SNAP food waivers have been signed to limit recipients’ ability to purchase unhealthy foods, and President Trump secured $50 billion in funding for rural hospitals.

  • PROMISE MADE: “We’ll take on the corruption at the FDA, the CDC, World Health Organization, and other institutions of public health that… are dominated by corporate power and dominated, really, by China.” (9/7/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: On Day One, President Trump signed an Executive Order withdrawing the nation from the World Health Organization and the U.S. formally exited the WHO on January 22, 2026.

  • PROMISE MADE: “I think vaccines are — certain vaccines — are incredible, but maybe some aren’t, and if they aren’t, we have to find out.” (12/8/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: At President Trump’s direction, the Department of Health and Human Services revised its childhood vaccine recommendations from 72 shots for 11 diseases to ten “consensus vaccines.”

  • PROMISE MADE: “Under the Trump Administration, your government will pay for, or your insurance company will be mandated to pay for all costs associated with IVF treatment…” (8/29/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump announced actions to lower costs and expand access to IVF — including a Most Favored Nation deal on fertility drugs that the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services estimates can save women up to $2,200 per cycle, alongside a new option for employers to offer fertility benefits.

Empowering Parents and Returning Education to the States

  • PROMISE MADE: “I will close the Department of Education and move all education back to the states where it belongs.” (8/4/23)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump directed the Secretary of Education to take all necessary steps to facilitate the closure of the Department of Education and return authority back where it was intended — with individual states and school districts, which are best equipped to make decisions that benefit their own unique constituencies. The Department of Education has already taken steps towards that goal, such as announcing the Department will move out of its D.C. headquarters, saving Americans over $4.8 million annually.

  • PROMISE MADE: “I will sign a new Executive Order to cut federal funding for any school pushing critical race theory … or political content onto the shoulders of our children.” (8/3/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump signed an order to defund schools promoting divisive critical race theory and radical gender ideology.

  • PROMISE MADE: “We want federal education dollars to follow the student, rather than propping up a bloated and radical bureaucracy in Washington, D.C.” (10/1/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump signed an Executive Order expanding educational freedom and opportunity for families — and the Working Families Tax Cuts created the Education Freedom Tax Credit, America’s first nationwide school choice program in which taxpayers can claim a credit of up to $1,700 — or $3,400 for married couples — for contributions that fund K-12 scholarships.

  • PROMISE MADE: “I will not give one penny to any school that has a vaccine mandate or a mask mandate.” (5/25/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump signed an Executive Order ensuring discretionary federal funds do not support schools that mandate students take the COVID-19 vaccine in order to attend in-person classes.

  • PROMISE MADE: “We will teach students to love their country, not to hate their country like they’re taught right now.” (9/13/23)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump reestablished the 1776 Commission to restore patriotic education in American public schools and ended federal support for radical indoctrination in the classroom.

  • PROMISE MADE: “We will support bringing back prayer to our schools.” (9/13/23)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump announced new protections for the right to pray in public schools and safeguarded students’ and teachers’ rights to protected prayer and religious expression.

Protecting Women, Children, and Biological Reality

  • PROMISE MADE: “As of today, it will henceforth be the official policy of the United States government that there are only two genders: male and female.” (1/20/25)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump declared it the official policy of the U.S. government that there are only two sexes: male and female.

  • PROMISE MADE: “We are not going to allow child sexual mutilation.” (11/18/23)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump successfully forced hospitals nationwide — including Stanford Medicine, Cleveland Clinic, Children’s Minnesota, and dozens of others — to abandon their so-called “gender-affirming care“ and chemical castration programs for kids in compliance with the Trump Administration’s order.

  • PROMISE MADE: “We will keep men out of women’s sports.” (5/26/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump immediately ended the unfair, demeaning practice of forcing women to compete against biological men in sports — which resulted in the NCAA changing its rules and the U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Committee banning men from competing in women’s sports. Additionally, countless states and high schools have also changed their policies to comply with the order.

Defending Free Speech, Faith, and the Constitution

  • PROMISE MADE: “We’re going to bust up the censorship regime and bring back free speech again” (1/28/23)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump signed Executive Orders dismantling censorship, protecting religious freedoms, and safeguarding Second Amendment rights, and immediately directed his Administration to take all necessary steps to defend Americans’ constitutional rights from overreach.

  • PROMISE MADE: “I will defend religious liberty.” (1/19/25)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: The Trump Administration directed all federal agencies to protect religious expression in the workplace, established the Religious Liberty Commission to identify threats to religious liberty and protect the free exercise of religion, and opened the first-ever White House Faith Office to empower faith-based entities, community organizations, and houses of worship to better serve families and communities.

  • PROMISE MADE: “Upon taking office, I will create a new federal task force on fighting anti-Christian bias.” (2/22/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump established the Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias at the Department of Justice to end the unlawful policies and practices that targeted Christians during prior Administrations — culminating in a report detailing Democrats’ radical efforts to punish Christians and highlighting President Trump’s efforts to restore religious liberty.

  • PROMISE MADE: “When I’m back in the Oval Office, no one will lay a finger on your firearms. It’s not going to happen.” (2/9/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump has not wavered in his support for Americans’ Second Amendment rights. In fact, the Working Families Tax Cuts eliminated the $200 federal tax on suppressors, short-barreled rifles, and short-barreled shotguns — a tax that had burdened law-abiding gun owners since 1934.

Restoring Safety and Free Speech to College Campuses

  • PROMISE MADE: “We will deport the foreign jihad sympathizers and Hamas supporters from our midst. We will get them out of our country.” (9/19/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump has cracked down on campus chaos with federal enforcement and visa revocations for pro-Hamas agitators — restoring safety, free speech, and American values to higher education nationwide. More than 300,000 visas have been revoked, including 6,000 from foreign students who committed crimes or have ties to terrorism.

  • PROMISE MADE: “When I return to the White House, I will fire the Radical Left accreditors that have allowed our colleges to become dominated by Marxist Maniacs and lunatics.” (7/17/23)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump ordered a sweeping overhaul of college accreditation and directed the Department of Education to hold accreditors accountable, up to and including the termination of their federal recognition, for lowering standards or enforcing illegal DEI discrimination, and to open the door to new accreditors.

  • PROMISE MADE: “My promise to Jewish Americans is this: With your vote, I will be your defender, your protector, and I will be the best friend Jewish Americans have ever had in the White House.” (9/19/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump signed an Executive Order to combat the explosion of anti-Semitism on college campuses and in our communities, and launched an aggressive campaign targeting institutions without adequate protections for Jewish students or failure to address the rising antisemitism on their campuses.

Securing Our Elections and Ensuring Only U.S. Citizens Can Vote

  • PROMISE MADE: “We will secure our elections — and they will be secure once and for all.” (10/13/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump signed sweeping orders to protect the integrity of American elections by banning foreign nationals from election interference, strengthening citizenship verification, prosecuting illegal voting, and requiring voter-verifiable paper ballot records. The Trump Administration also enhanced the SAVE system to ensure noncitizens cannot vote while moving to purge tens of thousands of illegal aliens from state voter rolls, and declassified hundreds of pages of intelligence records on threats to election security.

  • PROMISE MADE: “Ideally, we go to paper ballots, same-day voting, proof of citizenship, very big, and voter ID, very simple.” (8/29/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump is relentlessly fighting to pass the SAVE America Act, which would require proof of citizenship to register and a valid ID to vote in federal elections. The House passed the bill in February 2026, but Democrats continue to stand in the way; every Senate Democrat voted against commonsense voter ID — even though 84% of Americans support it. At the same time, the Trump Administration has taken historic action within the executive branch to strengthen voter integrity measures until the legislation passes.

Winning the Future in Super Intelligence, Digital Assets, and Space

  • PROMISE MADE: “We’re going to be way ahead on AI.” (12/12/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: The White House unveiled America’s AI Action Plan in order to secure American dominance in Super Intelligence and usher in the new Golden Age of human flourishing, competitiveness, and security. The Trump Administration is also protecting American households and businesses from rising electricity bills caused by the growth of data centers through the landmark Ratepayer Protection Pledge. And through the Genesis Mission, the Administration is harnessing Super Intelligence to drive scientific breakthroughs as part of more than $6 billion in new science investments.

  • PROMISE MADE: “We will repeal Joe Biden’s dangerous Executive Order that hinders AI Innovation, and imposes Radical Leftwing ideas on the development of this technology.” (7/8/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump revoked the Biden-era order on AI and directed his Administration to review and roll back every action taken under it, clearing away the barriers holding back American AI innovation. President Trump later renamed Artificial Intelligence as Super Intelligence.

  • PROMISE MADE: “I will also stop Joe Biden’s crusade to crush crypto. We’re going to stop it. I will ensure that the future of crypto and the future of Bitcoin will be made in the USA.” (5/26/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump signed the GENIUS Act into law, establishing a regulatory framework for stablecoins and helping ensure the U.S. remains the global leader in cryptocurrency, and unveiled a framework for achieving U.S. digital asset dominance — keeping President Trump’s promise to ensure the future of crypto is American.

  • PROMISE MADE: “This afternoon, I’m laying out my plan to ensure that the United States will be the crypto capital of the planet and the bitcoin superpower of the world.” (7/27/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump established the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and U.S. Digital Asset Stockpile — cementing America’s position as the crypto capital of the planet.

  • PROMISE MADE: “As your President, I will never allow the creation of a Central Bank Digital Currency.” (1/17/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump prohibited federal agencies from taking any action to establish, issue, or promote a Central Bank Digital Currency and ordered any ongoing plans terminated immediately, protecting Americans’ financial privacy from government surveillance.

  • PROMISE MADE: “We are also going to put in place strong protections to stop banks and regulators from trying to de-bank you for your political beliefs. That will never happen while I am your president.” (1/17/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump signed an Executive Order guaranteeing fair banking for all Americans — directing regulators to end politicized debanking and remove “reputation risk” from bank supervision.

  • PROMISE MADE: “…the other side is going to close it up, so if you like TikTok, go out and vote for Trump.” (9/4/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump saved TikTok, finalizing a historic deal that created a new majority American-owned joint venture to run the app in the U.S. while implementing comprehensive data protections and national security safeguards.

  • PROMISE MADE: “We will pursue our Manifest Destiny into the stars, launching American astronauts to plant the Stars and Stripes on the planet Mars.” (1/20/25)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: In April 2026, NASA’s Artemis II astronauts flew farther from Earth than any humans in history on the first crewed Moon mission in more than half a century. President Trump has directed NASA to return Americans to the Moon by 2028 and prepare for the journey to Mars.

Honoring American Greatness

  • PROMISE MADE: “We are going to be changing the name of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America — and we will restore the name of a great president, William McKinley, to Mount McKinley, where it should be and where it belongs.” (1/20/25)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump restored the name of Mount McKinley and renamed the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America — and he made English the official language of the United States.

  • PROMISE MADE: “I’m bringing Columbus Day back from the ashes… I am hereby reinstating Columbus Day under the same rules, dates, and locations, as it has had for all of the many decades before!” (4/27/25)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: In October 2025, President Trump proclaimed Columbus Day in honor of Christopher Columbus and installed a Columbus statue on the White House campus.

  • PROMISE MADE: “[We will] get rid of ugly buildings that are hurting those cities and other places and return to the magnificent classical style of Western civilization.” (3/25/23)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: President Trump mandated federal public buildings, such as courthouses and government office buildings, embrace classical architecture to honor tradition, foster civic pride, and inspire the citizenry. President Trump is also making Washington, D.C., beautiful again through projects and restorations.

Restoring Transparency and Accountability

  • PROMISE MADE: “We’re going to bring transparency and accountability back to our government.” (12/22/24)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: The Trump Administration has been the most transparent and accessible in modern American history, with President Trump taking unscripted questions multiple times per week and holding an unprecedented number of press conferences and interviews. Under President Trump, the briefing room dramatically increased the scope of its credentialed reporters, ensuring all Americans are in touch with their government.

  • PROMISE MADE: “We are going to make public remaining records relating to the assassinations of President John F. Kennedy, his brother, Robert Kennedy, as well as Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.” (1/19/25)
  • ✅ PROMISE KEPT: The Trump Administration has released troves of classified records, including documents related to the assassinations of President John F. Kennedy, Senator Robert F. Kennedy, and Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., as well as UFO/UAPs and Amelia Earhart.

President Trump has kept more promises, at greater speed, than any President in modern American history. From securing the border to cutting taxes to restoring Peace through Strength, the results are unmistakable — and the best is yet to come.

President Trump has delivered historic wins for America’s fishing industry by putting American fishermen first, unlocking billions of dollars in economic growth, revitalizing the industry, and providing critical regulatory relief.

Just one week ago, the Trump Administration unveiled its historic America First Seafood Strategy and launched Seafood.gov, to ensure that American fishermen, workers, industry, and coastal communities thrive from Alaska to Maine. The Trump Administration’s strategy is simple: end federal policies that punished American producers and rewarded foreign dependence. 

President Trump wasted no time in implementing important elements of his America First Seafood Strategy by announcing the new “U.S. Caught Seafood” voluntary label and making available more than $5 billion in guaranteed loans to expand American meat and seafood processing. 

Here’s what they’re saying:

  • Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick: “The species managed in U.S. waters are American icons – from Maine lobster to Gulf shrimp, from Alaskan salmon to Florida stone crab, American seafood is a rich part of U.S. history and our vibrant coastal economy. The America First Seafood Strategy ensures that the future of seafood in the United States will be built by American fishermen, American workers, and American industry—not by foreign imports.”
  • Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy Jr.: “I spent 40 years working for the commercial fishermen in this country, and commercial fishermen in this country have the strongest environmental regulations and the greatest sustainability regulations, but it puts them at a disadvantage to all the other fishermen in the world… President Trump is rebuilding the infrastructure and reopening the markets for our commercial fishermen.”
  • Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins: “AMERICAN SEAFOOD FIRST! 🇺🇸🦞 For too long, foreign imports have undercut American fishermen and workers. Under @POTUS, we’re changing that with [the] launch of the America First Seafood Strategy. Rebuilding American fisheries. Strengthening domestic production. Putting American fishermen FIRST. It’s time for American seafood to WIN in American markets!”
  • National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett: “It’s 100% true that the welfare of Maine growers and Maine fishermen, and especially the fishermen in Alaska, has been a key focus of this White House, and that message has been delivered.”
  • United Catcher Boats: “[W]e’re pleased to see the Trump Administration recognizing the importance of American-caught seafood and the fishermen who harvest it! America’s seafood economy supports jobs, families, and coastal communities across the country. And Alaska is at the heart of it… We appreciate the Administration’s leadership in bringing attention to these challenges and introducing the new voluntary U.S. Caught Seafood label, helping consumers recognize seafood harvested by American fishermen aboard U.S.-flagged vessels.”
  • North Carolina Fishermen’s Association Chair Brent Fulcher: “President Trump has brought more attention to the problems facing U.S. fishermen than any other in my lifetime. This plan coordinates multiple federal agencies to support U.S. seafood producers in fixing complex, long-term problems. It is a powerful step needed to rebuild America’s ability to produce seafood for generations to come, and I look forward to seeing the results.”
  • Alaska Marine Community Coalition Executive Director Michelle Stratton: “Investing in American seafood means investing in the people and places that keep this country fed… We thank the Administration for making fishing communities a national priority and recognizing their importance to America’s economic future.”
  • New England Fishermen’s Stewardship Association Director of Advocacy Jason Joyce: “The U.S. Caught Seafood label is a major win for consumers, American fishermen, seafood processors, and retailers alike. Our fishermen comply with some of the highest regulatory, health, safety, and environmental standards in the world, and consumers deserve to know that their seafood is harvested safely and sustainably by American fishermen. We believe U.S. seafood is the most sustainably harvested in the world, and this label gives consumers a simple, recognizable way to identify American-caught seafood while supporting our domestic fishing, processing, and retail industries.”
  • Maine Coast Fishermen’s Association Executive Director Ben Martens: “A strong fishing industry needs vessels and ports that can carry it into the future… We welcome the attention to fleet and port modernization and access to financing. These are practical investments in safer operations, stronger businesses, and waterfronts that can continue serving their communities for generations.”
  • National Seafood Association President and CEO Lisa Wallenda Picard: “The National Seafood Association applauds the Trump Administration for recognizing the essential role seafood plays in America’s economic health and public health. A robust commercial seafood sector and an emphasis on affordable, healthy, protein-focused nutrition work together to benefit Americans.

    “We see great promise in a holistic plan that prioritizes rebuilding infrastructure, eliminating regulatory barriers, and encouraging investment in the commercial seafood sector.

    “As global sourcing plays an indispensable role in feeding American families and keeping seafood processing and distribution workers in this country employed, the strategy’s emphasis on these priorities is spot on.  We look forward to working with the Administration on its effort to promote America’s iconic catch and drive consumption of the healthiest animal protein on the planet.”
  • New England Young Fishermen’s Alliance Executive Director Andrea Tomlinson: “We are excited to see national attention on the businesses and communities where the next generation will build their careers, and we look forward to helping turn that momentum into lasting opportunities for young fishermen.”
  • Southern Shrimp Alliance Executive Director Blake Price: “President Trump has prioritized getting fishermen back to work to supply Americans with healthy, sustainable, domestically-sourced seafood. The U.S. shrimp industry is thrilled to see a detailed America First Seafood Strategy and looks forward to assisting federal agencies in the implementation of its objectives.” 
  • Fishing Communities Coalition: “The Fishing Communities Coalition (FCC) welcomes the America First Seafood Strategy and thanks the Trump Administration and its federal agency partners for recognizing American fishermen as essential food producers and investing in the future of the communities they sustain. 

    “The strategy brings together priorities critical to fishing businesses nationwide: strengthening domestic markets, modernizing vessels and working waterfronts, improving access to financing, combating illegal fishing and unfair competition, and supporting fisheries management informed by current science. For FCC’s community-based fishing organizations, this coordinated attention represents an important opportunity to strengthen America’s seafood system from the water to the dinner table.”
  • Gulf of America Reef Fish Shareholders’ Alliance Deputy Director Eric Brazer: “We welcome the strategy’s focus on leveling the playing field, applaud the renewed focus on marketing our high-quality products to consumers who value buying American, and thank the Administration for standing behind the fishermen who supply this country with responsibly harvested seafood.”  
  • Commercial Fishermen of Santa Barbara Executive Director Kim Selkoe: “We welcome the emphasis on promoting American seafood in export markets alongside the infrastructure needed to land it in our ports and deliver it throughout the supply chain. Local docks, ice, cold storage, and processing connect fishermen to customers near and far. Supporting those connections helps more of the value of each catch stay in the community.”

The U.S. economy grew at a strong annual rate of 3.4% in the third quarter of 2026 — the strongest pace in a year. President Donald J. Trump’s America First agenda is delivering as promised: faster growth, historic levels of investment, and an economy that continues to outperform the so-called “experts.”

Here’s what you need to know:

  • Businesses are investing big in America. Private investment in plants and equipment surged at a 9.4% rate in the third quarter, accelerating from an already strong second quarter. So far this year, investment is growing more than twice as fast as it did in 2025 and three times faster than the weak 2.3% rate in Biden’s final year. That means more factories, more manufacturing, more jobs, and more production here at home.
  • Business investment just posted its strongest quarter in nearly 15 years. With growth of almost 13% in the third quarter, it’s a clear signal that companies are betting on American workers, factories, and production under President Trump.
  • Strong momentum is building. Over the past three quarters, the economy has grown at a 2.7% rate — faster than the Blue Chip consensus forecast (2.4%) and well above the Congressional Budget Office’s projection (2.2%).
  • The “experts” were wrong — again. 72% of the economists surveyed by Bloomberg underestimated today’s growth number, once again missing the strength of the Trump economy.
  • American consumers remain resilient. Consumer spending grew at a solid 3.8% rate last quarter as American families spend with confidence and businesses expand.
  • America is investing in its future. Capital goods — the equipment and machinery that build American industry — now make up a record share of U.S. imports. At the same time, consumer goods fell to just 17% of goods imports, tied for the lowest level on record. Combined with the surge in domestic investment, this shows President Trump’s policies are helping rebuild American productive capacity.

President Trump’s agenda of lower taxes, fewer regulations, energy dominance, and America First trade are fueling a historic investment boom that is powering strong growth. Businesses are betting on America, and the foundation of the future is being built right here at home.

The Government of the United States of America and the Government of Finland (hereinafter referred to as the “Participants”),

Expressing mutual interest in science and technology capabilities and standards to usher in the next Golden Age of Innovation to fortify freedom and prosperity for generations to come,

Affirming the value of bilateral science and technology collaboration to enrich the lives and livelihoods of citizens in both countries, and to elevate the U.S.-Finland Alliance to a higher level,

Building on the longstanding collaboration established under the existing Agreement Relating to Scientific and Technological Cooperation between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Republic of Finland, done at Washington May 16, 1995,

Taking note of the Joint Statement of the United States and Finland on Cooperation in Quantum Information Science and Technology and also the Joint Statement of the United States and Finland on Cooperation in Advanced Wireless Communications, and

Recognizing the importance of deepening ties with strategic partners as a means to strengthen stability, security, and competitiveness,

Have reached the following understandings:

I. Purpose

The purpose of this Memorandum of Understanding (hereinafter “MOU”) is to enable collaboration towards joint opportunities of mutual interest in strategic science and technology disciplines with a focus on strengthening industrial cooperation and accelerating the development, deployment, and adoption of emerging technologies to power the next generation of global connectivity, secure quantum advantage, advance energy leadership, develop advanced semiconductors, strengthen space collaboration, advance an open and secure super intelligence (SI) stack, accelerate secure biotechnology innovation, strengthen research and industrial security, and advance shipbuilding modernization and Arctic technology cooperation.[1]

II. Areas of Cooperation

The Participants aim to collaborate in a number of disciplines, including but not limited to the following:

Accelerating Development and Diffusion of the Trusted Technology Stack in SI and Connectivity

Recognizing the importance of secure and trusted technology infrastructure to economic prosperity and national security, the Participants intend to deepen cooperation to advance next-generation SI and network technologies. The Participants intend to collaborate on telecommunications R&D, promote and finance the export of trusted technology stacks, and coordinate on international standards development.

Focus areas for collaboration are intended to include:

  • Promoting development and exports across the full SI and network technology stack, including hardware, models, software, applications, network equipment, maintenance, long-term customer support, and related standards;
  • Partnering to finance trusted technology stack exports and to provide customer support to accelerate adoption in third-party countries by coordinating, as appropriate, applicable U.S. and Finnish financing and commercial diplomacy tools to support competitive deployments in priority third-country markets;
  • Shaping telecommunications standards in line with shared priorities through coordinated engagement in international standards bodies including the International Telecommunication Union, the Global Coalition on Telecommunications, and partnership with industry at 3GPP;
  • Collaborating to shape resolutions in advance of all major ITU decision-making conferences, including the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference and 2026 ITU Plenipotentiary;
  • Strengthening existing research and development in 5G and 6G and next-generation communication technologies through accelerated pathways from research and development to commercial and industrial deployment, and strengthened industrial cooperation; and
  • Building trusted, secure, interoperable 5G and 6G supply chains and advocating for policies that accelerate adoption of trusted connectivity infrastructure.

Securing Quantum Advantage

The Participants recognize that quantum technologies are poised to deliver transformative advances across economic and national security domains. Sustained leadership in quantum innovation depends on secure supply chains, strong research and industrial ecosystems, and close collaboration between trusted partners. The Participants intend to deepen cooperation to accelerate the development, commercialization, and responsible deployment of quantum technologies in ways that enhance prosperity and security.

Focus areas for collaboration are intended to include:

  • Collaborating through leading quantum institutions and national laboratories to assess quantum performance, develop quantum algorithms, and enable scientific discovery, including by advancing hybrid quantum-classical computing;
  • Accelerating commercial deployment of cryogenics, precision instrumentation and semiconductor process engineering firms through regulatory harmonization efforts and targeted investments in Finland and in the United States;
  • Supporting the development of the next generation of scientists and engineers through joint research and investments into quantum manufacturing;
  • Aligning efforts to secure technology and supply chains and to build a trusted ecosystem for the research, development, and adoption of new quantum technologies;
  • Strengthening pathways for information sharing and establishing commercial pipelines between U.S. and Finnish stakeholders to accelerate the commercialization of quantum technologies and bolster the alignment between the two commercial quantum ecosystems;
  • Cooperating on trusted quantum ecosystem development by aligning efforts focused on secure quantum supply chains and informing coordinated engagement in Quantum Development Group (QDG), Multilateral Dialogue on Quantum (MDQ), and NATO Transatlantic Quantum Community (TQC) engagement;
  • Advancing trusted, interoperable standards for quantum technologies through existing complementary multilateral and bilateral pre-standardization activities as relevant in quantum computing, sensing, and networking; and
  • Endorsing and advocating for the adoption of Post-Quantum Cryptographic standards and supporting the migration of systems to those standards, as well as advancing R&D and commercial cooperation in encryption technology capabilities and strengthening trade and exports in the sector by cyber security companies.

Unlocking Energy Innovation and Resilience

The Participants are strengthening cooperation to advance secure, resilient and diversified energy systems. Together we are expanding energy collaboration across SMR development and deployment, nuclear fission R&D, geothermal, and energy resilience, to support innovation and the reliable deployment of next-generation energy infrastructure.

Focus areas for collaboration are intended to include:

  • Strengthening civil nuclear energy cooperation to accelerate the development and commercial deployment of American and Finnish nuclear reactors, including small modular reactors (SMRs), and expand collaboration on regulatory harmonization;
  • Advancing cooperation on nuclear lifecycle innovation including repository engineering, encapsulation of used nuclear fuel, nuclear monitoring technologies and SI-enabled geologic modeling;
  • Advancing collaboration on geothermal technologies including the research, development and deployment of advanced drilling, subsurface characterization, and enhanced geothermal systems;
  • Advancing development of the secure supply of advanced energy systems, including bulk power components and energy storage devices;
  • Advancing cooperation on advanced manufacturing including rare-earth-free magnets, high-efficiency motors, advanced batteries, and advanced materials;
  • Advancing cooperation on fusion technologies such as fusion fuel cycle and blanket integration systems, neutronics modeling, and fusion materials; and
  • Promoting innovation in critical minerals technologies including the sensing, characterization, extraction, processing and recovery of critical minerals and advanced materials essential to energy systems.

Strengthening Space Collaboration

Recognizing that bilateral cooperation on space benefits both countries’ national interests, the Participants intend to deepen cooperation and engage in dialogue on space security, space exploration, and space technology research, development, and commercialization.

Focus areas for collaboration are intended to include:

  • Continuing the partnership on space science and exploration, including potential collaboration on future Artemis lunar surface exploration missions and beyond;
  • Facilitating cooperation between commercial actors from the United States and Finland, supporting growth of space companies from both countries and building on complementary strengths;
  • Facilitating commercial and civil space cooperation by addressing regulatory burdens on commercial space activities and advocating for policies that can adapt to technical development, business innovation, and market demands; and
  • Leveraging our geostrategic locations as space nations to promote Arctic security and prosperity.

Advancing Defense Innovation

Building on the above-mentioned areas with dual-use applications and the existing defense agreements, the Participants intend to pursue joint research projects, conduct pilot activities, and explore pathways for scaling promising technologies from research and demonstration to operational and industrial deployment.

Advancing Biomedical, Biotechnological, and Advanced Material Innovation

Recognizing the importance of advancing biotechnological research, including in biomedical and biomanufacturing fields, accelerating materials innovation through super intelligence, and securing biotechnology and health supply chains, the Participants intend to:

  • Leverage insights derived from nationally governed health and research data infrastructures to advance precision medicine research and clinical research readiness, while reinforcing shared commitments to research and industrial security, trusted data infrastructure, and resilience against adversary-linked dependencies;
  • Strengthen research and development and accelerate innovation and adoption of new solutions rooted in biotechnology broadly across supply chains and ecosystems; and
  • Enhance research that combines computational, experimental, and data-based capabilities to accelerate the discovery, design, and validation of new materials.

Advancing Arctic Technology and Operational Capability

Recognizing the strategic importance of the Arctic to shared security, prosperity, and resilience, the Participants intend to support close collaboration on Arctic operations, ice navigation, maritime domain awareness, cold-weather testing, and enabling technologies. Recognizing Finland’s established leadership in icebreaker design and construction, the Participants intend to collaborate on icebreaker modernization efforts and related shipyard and workforce development.

The Participants intend to accelerate industrial cooperation and to modernize the United States’ icebreaker fleet under ICE Pact, leveraging Finnish expertise to support the secure and timely design, construction, and delivery of next-generation Arctic Security Cutters (ASCs). Expanding this framework, the Participants intend to explore possibilities to deepen their collaboration in ship design and shipbuilding technologies, processes, and shipyard management. Furthermore, the Participants intend to jointly invest in enabling technologies such as SI-driven manufacturing, ice technology, unmanned systems, and space-enabled situational awareness.

The Participants recognize the strategic importance of advancing Arctic connectivity including both satellite and submarine communication services. The Participants intend to advocate policies and commercial cooperation that enhance satellite coverage at high latitudes and support the establishment of subsea communication cables in the Arctic region, thereby strengthening connectivity between North America and Northern Europe and, eventually, the Indo-Pacific region.

Strengthening Security in Research and Industry

Recognizing the importance of shared research integrity and security across critical and emerging technology research and development, the Participants intend to strengthen continued collaboration to protect their technologies, their critical supply chains, and their people. The Participants intend to collaborate on research and industry security, and to identify and mitigate threats to both the research enterprise and private sector research and development.

Focus areas for collaboration are intended to include:

  • Strengthening security in research and industry through intellectual property security, investment screening, and partnerships;
  • Building trusted science and innovation ecosystems by mitigating high-risk entity participation in sensitive science and technology R&D activities;
  • Strengthening safeguards and enforcement mechanisms for government-funded research and talent programs by enhancing disclosure of foreign funding and affiliations in order to mitigate and address security risks related to partnerships with entities of shared security concerns;
  • Establishing a bilateral research security dialogue and information exchange on threats, cases, risk assessments, mitigation efforts, and entities of security concern;
  • Collaborating with allies and partners to adopt enhanced research security practices to facilitate a trusted innovation ecosystem;
  • Enhancing transparency and due diligence across the innovation ecosystem by strengthening vetting of research institutions, researchers, partnerships, and funding and implementing safeguards against foreign interference and malign talent recruitment; and
  • Applying shared research integrity and security principles across TPD workstreams to guide collaboration, protect sensitive R&D activities, and inform future research and industrial security programming.

III. Operation and Discontinuation

1.   This MOU becomes operative on the date of the last signature. The Participants may modify this MOU by written mutual decision. Either Participant may discontinue this MOU at any time by providing written notice of discontinuation to the other Participant. The discontinuation is expected to commence on a date 180 days after the date on which notice of discontinuation is delivered. The Participants intend to advance the implementation of the MOU through the Joint Committee Meeting mechanism. The Participants intend to leverage, as appropriate, the Science and Technology Agreement as an operational framework for implementation of this MOU.

2.   This MOU does not constitute or create and is not intended to constitute or create any legally binding obligations. Nothing in this MOU is intended to alter or affect any existing agreements between the Participants.

3.   Cooperation under this MOU is intended to take place in accordance with the Participants’ applicable national legislation and international obligations, including, for Finland, applicable current and future European Union coordination, laws, and regulations, and without prejudice to the Participants’ respective regulatory processes.

4.   Nothing in this MOU commits the Participants to the expenditure of funds.

5.   Activities involving personal data are intended to comply with applicable data-protection frameworks. Nothing in this MOU authorizes the disclosure or transfer of classified, controlled, confidential business, or proprietary information. Matters involving the ownership, protection, access, use, licensing, or commercialization of intellectual property are expected to be addressed through separate implementing arrangements or project-specific agreements, as appropriate.

6.   The foregoing represents the understanding reached between the Participants on the matters referred to in this MOU.

Signed in Washington, D.C. on October 29 in English.

[1] In Finland, ‘super intelligence’ refers to ‘artificial intelligence’

Today, President Donald J. Trump returns to the Buckeye State to showcase a record of results that puts Ohio workers, families, seniors, farmers, and communities first. Under the leadership of President Trump and Republicans, Ohioans are benefiting from historic tax relief, falling crime, surging private investment, stronger rural healthcare, and new resources for the state’s defense industry.

Delivering Historic Tax Relief for Ohioans

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts are putting real money back in the pockets of hardworking Ohio workers, families, and seniors.

  • No Tax on Overtime: More than 1.2 million Ohio workers claimed $3.4 billion in No Tax on Overtime deductions in 2026.
  • No Tax on Social Security: More than 1.5 million Ohio seniors benefited from the new senior deduction in 2026, with the average senior expected to pay zero federal taxes on Social Security benefits.
  • Bigger Refunds: Ohio taxpayers saw average refunds of $3,308 in 2026.
  • Protecting Jobs and Wages: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 208,000 Ohio jobs, $37 billion in state GDP, and $19 billion in wages for Ohioans.
  • Lowering Taxes for Small Businesses and Family Farms: The tax cuts permanently locked in the increased death tax exemption (indexed for inflation), 100% expensing, a doubled Section 179 limit, and the 20% small business deduction. They also expanded crop insurance and raised reference prices for the first time in over a decade.

Strengthening Rural Healthcare Across Ohio

President Trump is delivering targeted resources to expand access, modernize care, and improve outcomes in Ohio’s rural communities.

  • Rural Health Transformation: Ohio secured more than $200 million in first-year funding under the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Rural Health Transformation Program.
  • Modernizing Care: The Trump Administration awarded $92 million across 22 rural Ohio hospitals to support coordinated care networks, maternal health services, and equipment and facilities upgrades.

Making Ohio Communities Safer

Violent crime is falling across Ohio as President Trump’s law and order agenda takes hold.

  • Statewide homicides dropped 16.1% last year.
  • Columbus hit a 16-year low in homicides in 2025, with further declines in 2026.
  • Cincinnati saw homicides fall more than 6% in 2025 and drop another 19% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period the year before.
  • Cleveland recorded double-digit drops in 2025: homicides down 16%, rapes down 28%, auto thefts down 26%, and robberies down 24%. In the first half of 2026, rapes fell another 8% and robberies another 21%.

Unleashing Private Investment and Job Creation

President Trump’s pro-growth, America First policies are drawing major private investment and new jobs across the Buckeye State.

  • Nvidia is financing up to $105 billion for a new Super Intelligence data center in Pike County.
  • Electra is investing $850 million to open its first EL9 Ultra Short aircraft production facility in Springfield, creating 1,975 new jobs.
  • Stellantis is investing $400 million in its Toledo Assembly Complex, creating over 900 jobs.
  • Bayer is investing $2.2 billion to build a pharmaceutical manufacturing campus in New Albany, creating about 600 permanent jobs and 1,500 construction jobs.
  • Honda is investing up to $2.5 billion to build a new hybrid vehicle production plant in Ohio. 
  • Hikma Pharmaceuticals is investing $267 million to expand its manufacturing facilities in Columbus and Bedford, creating 350 new jobs.
  • Weidmann is investing $150 million to renovate and expand a historic former paper mill in Middletown, creating dozens of new full-time jobs.
  • Kreate is investing $100 million for a new consumer and professional plastic products manufacturing facility in Tiffin.
  • Kimberly-Clark is investing $800 million to build its first new U.S. plant in 37 years in Warren.
  • Vallourec is investing $48 million to expand its operations in Youngstown.

Powering Growth and Protecting Communities

President Trump is securing reliable energy and delivering for communities that were neglected under the previous Administration.

  • Protecting Ratepayers: The Trump Administration formed a public-private partnership with SoftBank Group and SB Energy to build 10 gigawatts of new power generation in southern Ohio, ensuring corporations — not Ohio families — pay the costs of data center growth. The deal includes $40 million in community benefits from SB Energy.
  • Standing Up for East Palestine: After years of inaction, the Trump Administration launched a five-year, $10 million research initiative to study the long-term health impacts of the 2023 train derailment and ensure residents receive the medical attention they need.
  • Revitalizing American Steelmaking: The Trump Administration awarded $500 million to support a $1 billion investment at Cleveland-Cliffs’ Middletown Works facility in Middletown, protecting 2,300 jobs and strengthening our domestic steel supply chain.

Strengthening Ohio’s Defense Industry

President Trump is expanding Ohio’s role in national security and high-tech defense manufacturing.

  • In October, President Trump announced that Cleveland will be home to the new U.S. Submarine Component Repair Center.
  • The first Ohio-built Fury fighter drone for the U.S. Air Force rolled off the line in July at Anduril’s Arsenal-1 plant in Pickaway County — a $910.5 million project expected to create more than 4,000 jobs.
  • The FY 2026 NDAA provided more than $72 million for Ohio defense projects, including $60 million for work at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base.

President Trump and Republicans are delivering for Ohio families, workers, seniors, and communities — proving once again that America First means Ohio First. Ohioans face a clear choice: continue this progress or return to the higher taxes, open borders, and failed policies of the past.

President Donald J. Trump returns to Florida today to highlight a clear record of results that puts hardworking Americans first. Under President Trump and Republican leadership, Floridians are seeing historic tax relief, a surge in private investment and job creation, stronger rural healthcare, accelerated infrastructure and environmental progress, expanded support for veterans, and safer communities.

Delivering Tax Relief for Hardworking Floridians

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts are putting real money back in the pockets of Sunshine State workers, families, and seniors.

  • No Tax on Social Security: Approximately 4.8 million Florida seniors benefit from the new senior deduction, with the average senior expected to pay zero federal taxes on Social Security benefits.
  • Bigger Refunds: Florida taxpayers saw average refunds of $4,433 in 2026 — the highest of any state.
  • Protecting Jobs and Wages: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 399,000 Florida jobs, $73 billion in state GDP, and $36 billion in workers’ wages.
  • Expanding Workforce Opportunity: In September 2026, the Trump Administration approved Florida’s Workforce Pell Grant program, enabling students at Eastern Florida State College and other institutions to use Pell Grant funding for high-demand careers such as firefighting, corrections, and emergency management.

Unleashing Private Investment and Job Creation

President Trump’s pro-growth, America First policies are attracting significant private capital and creating high-quality jobs across Florida.

  • Johnson & Johnson is investing $1 billion to upgrade manufacturing and packaging technologies and build a new state-of-the-art distribution facility in Jacksonville.
  • Williams International is investing $1 billion to build a high-volume aviation gas turbine engine manufacturing facility in Okaloosa County.
  • Blue Origin is investing $600 million to expand its Rocket Park campus at Cape Canaveral Spaceport.
  • Lupin is investing $250 million to construct a new pharmaceutical manufacturing plant in Coral Springs.
  • Chick-fil-A is investing $150 million to build a new distribution center in Winter Haven.
  • Monin is investing $111 million to build a manufacturing plant in Zephyrhills.
  • Tampa Brass & Aluminum is investing $58 million in machinery and equipment at its Tampa headquarters.

Strengthening Rural Healthcare Access

President Trump is delivering targeted resources to expand and modernize care in Florida’s rural communities.

  • Florida secured $210 million in first-year funding through the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Rural Health Transformation Program — the largest federal investment in rural healthcare in American history.
  • In August 2026, the state awarded $188 million in Rural Health Transformation Program grants across 31 rural counties. These funds support expanded access to care, growth of the rural healthcare workforce, preventive and home-based services, specialty and acute care, value-based care models, rural and satellite clinics, and health and lifestyle initiatives.

Investing in Florida’s Infrastructure and Natural Resources

President Trump is accelerating critical projects that protect Florida’s communities and natural resources while strengthening the state’s economy and readiness.

  • Accelerating Everglades Restoration: Working with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the Trump Administration modified key contracts to expedite the Everglades Agricultural Area Reservoir. The project is now on track for completion by 2029 — five years ahead of the previous timeline — improving water distribution to the Everglades, protecting drinking water supplies, and reducing harmful discharges.
  • Upgrading Critical Infrastructure: In October 2026, the Trump Administration awarded $85 million to upgrade 20 miles of I-4 highway between State Road 434 and State Road 472 in Seminole and Volusia counties. In August 2026, the Trump Administration awarded over $1 million to the Gulf Marine Corporation in Tampa for training center equipment, wheel loaders, and upgrades to three berths. In May 2026, the Federal Aviation Administration awarded President Donald J. Trump International Airport $10 million to expand the terminal and add new facilities for mothers and travelers with special needs.
  • Advancing Roadway Safety: Through Operation Highway Shield, the Trump Administration partnered with state and local law enforcement to conduct more than 3,300 inspections across Florida in just one month, focusing on unqualified foreign drivers operating commercial vehicles. 176 drivers were placed out of service, including 54 for language deficiencies, while dozens of others were arrested on criminal charges and immigration violations.
  • Delivering Disaster Relief: The Trump Administration has moved quickly to support Florida communities struck by disaster. In October 2026, President Trump authorized FEMA coordination following Hurricane Isaias. Earlier actions included more than $116 million to accelerate recovery after extreme storms, an increase in the federal cost-share for Hurricane Michael recovery, and nearly $416 million in additional disaster relief.
  • Funding Rail Safety: In September 2025, the Trump Administration released $42 million in four grants for critical rail safety projects along the Brightline corridor after the projects had been stalled in the Biden Administration’s backlog.
  • Advancing American Space Leadership: Artemis II launched from Florida’s Space Coast in April 2026. Artemis III is also scheduled to launch from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center, reinforcing Florida’s central role in America’s return to the Moon and beyond.

Honoring and Supporting Florida Veterans

President Trump is expanding resources that strengthen care, housing stability, and prevention services for the heroes who have served our nation.

  • In October 2026, the VA awarded more than $600,000 to Florida community organizations for adaptive sports programs that help veterans build independence, well-being, and quality of life.
  • In September 2026, the VA awarded more than $113 million in grants to 42 Florida organizations to assist veterans who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless.
  • The VA also awarded more than $6 million to 12 Florida organizations providing suicide prevention services to veterans.
  • In June 2026, the VA broke ground on a new clinic in North Port that will replace the Port Charlotte clinic and serve more than 10,000 veterans annually.

Making Florida Safer and More Secure

President Trump is delivering decisive action that is driving down crime in Florida communities while securing the border and ending the failed policies of the past.

  • Historic Drops in Violent Crime: Violent crime declined across Florida last year, with murders down 19%. In Miami, in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025, homicides plunged 50%, rapes dropped 22%, robberies fell 22%, and aggravated assaults declined 8%.
  • Securing the Border: The Trump Administration awarded Florida $608 million to expand illegal alien detention capacity. Catch-and-release has been fully ended, producing 17 straight months of zero releases at the border and zero Border Patrol releases in FY2026 — the first fiscal year in history with that result. Illegal southern border crossings were slashed by 95% from Biden-era levels in FY2026, the lowest total on record. Refugee admissions have also been sharply reduced.

President Trump and Republicans are delivering lower taxes, major private investment, stronger rural healthcare, critical infrastructure, expanded veteran support, and safer communities. Floridians face a clear choice: continue this progress or return to higher taxes, open borders, and the failed policies of the past.

Delivering Historic Tax Relief for Iowans

President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts are delivering real relief to Hawkeye State workers, families, farmers, and seniors.

  • No Tax on Social Security: Approximately 600,000 Iowa seniors benefit from the new senior deduction, with the average senior expected to pay zero federal taxes on Social Security benefits.

  • Protecting Jobs and Wages: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 57,000 Iowa jobs, $10 billion in state GDP, and $5 billion in workers’ wages.
  • Lowering Taxes for Family Farms: The Working Families Tax Cuts made the increased death tax exemption permanent and indexed it for inflation, helping keep generational farms in the family. The package also made 100% expensing permanent, doubled the Section 179 limit, made the 20% small business deduction permanent, expanded crop insurance, and increased reference prices for the first time in over a decade.
  • Expanding Workforce Grants: In August 2026, the Trump Administration approved the nation’s first Workforce Pell Grant program, allowing students at Iowa Central Community College to use Pell dollars for the Emergency Medical Technician program.

Standing with Iowa Farmers and Producers

President Trump’s America First agenda is delivering direct support, lower costs, and expanded markets to the farmers and producers who feed the country.

  • Year-Round E15 and Stronger Biofuels: In 2025, the Trump Administration cleared summer sales of E15 nationwide, waived all federal barriers to E10, and implemented the highest-ever renewable fuel volume requirements.
  • Historic Production: In 2025, Iowa farmers posted the state’s second-highest corn yield, a record corn production (2.77 billion bushels), a record soybean yield, and its third-highest soybean production.
  • Direct Relief: USDA has delivered more than $833 million to 57,000 Iowa farmers through the Emergency Commodity Assistance Program and more than $867 million in Farmer Bridge Assistance payments. The Trump Administration also announced an $8 billion Harvest Fuel Relief program to help address temporary higher input costs and market disruptions.
  • Reducing Costs: President Trump suspended certain phosphate fertilizer duties, designated phosphate and potash as critical minerals, extended a Jones Act waiver to improve fertilizer logistics, and launched the $500 million FIELDS Program to expand domestic fertilizer production. The Administration also temporarily allowed off-road dyed diesel for highway use and deferred the federal excise tax to lower fuel costs.
  • Expanding Market Access: Ethanol exports reached a record high in 2025, up 13% from the year prior and 18% since President Trump returned to office, while U.S. food and agricultural exports have risen under expanded global market access.
  • Cutting Red Tape: President Trump’s “Right to Repair” effort allows farmers to lawfully repair their equipment, saving thousands of dollars per repair. The Administration also fixed diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) system issues that were forcing farm equipment and trucks to derate or shut down.

Strengthening Rural Healthcare Across Iowa

President Trump is directing targeted resources to expand access and modernize care in Iowa’s rural communities.

  • Rural Health Transformation: Iowa secured $209 million in first-year funding through the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Rural Health Transformation Program to expand clinical services, strengthen the rural health workforce, modernize technology and infrastructure, and improve coordination.
  • Modernizing Local Facilities: Funding from the program is supporting upgrades that include an MRI at Lucas County Health Center, a PET/CT system and new providers at Mahaska Health, a robotic bronchoscopy system at North Iowa Medical Center, expanded prenatal care at Sioux Center Health, a new CT scanner at Washington County Hospital, and a radiation oncology center at Wayne County Hospital.

Unleashing Private Investment and High-Quality Jobs

President Trump’s pro-growth, America First agenda is driving major private investment and job creation across Iowa.

  • Mesabi Metallics announced a $15 billion investment to build a major steelmaking complex in Lee County, creating thousands of construction jobs and at least 1,750 permanent positions.
  • John Deere announced a $20 billion U.S. investment, including new high-horsepower tractor assembly lines at its Waterloo plant.
  • Google announced a $7 billion investment in cloud and Super Intelligence infrastructure in Iowa, including a new data center in Cedar Rapids and expansion in Council Bluffs.
  • Kraft Heinz announced a $3 billion investment in its U.S. manufacturing operations, including its Davenport distribution center.
  • JBS USA announced a $135 million investment in a production facility in Perry, expected to create hundreds of jobs.
  • Electrical Power Products announced a $42 million expansion of its engineered-to-order electrical power control and protection systems manufacturing facility in Des Moines, creating 200 jobs.
  • Greater Machining and Manufacturing announced a $16 million expansion in Independence, creating 100 jobs.
  • Webster City Custom Meats announced a $2.5 million expansion of its meat processing facility in Webster City.
  • S&J Tube announced a $2.4 million expansion in Wapello.
  • Protecting Ratepayers: Under President Trump’s Ratepayer Protection Pledge, data center developers partnering with Alliant Energy, including QTS, must cover 100% of the energy and infrastructure costs for their facilities while supporting a five-year rate freeze for Iowans.
  • Restarting Duane Arnold: The Trump Administration announced a loan of up to $1.9 billion to NextEra to restart the Duane Arnold Energy Center, bringing Iowa’s only nuclear plant back online with 615 megawatts of baseload power — enough for nearly 500,000 homes.

Honoring and Supporting Iowa Veterans

President Trump is delivering targeted resources that strengthen care, housing stability, and prevention services for the veterans who have served our country.

  • In October 2026, the VA awarded funding to Iowa community organizations providing suicide prevention services to veterans.
  • In February 2026, the Iowa City VA Health Care System announced infrastructure upgrades, including a renovation of its dialysis unit, to support safe and effective patient care.
  • In September 2025, the VA awarded funding to five Iowa organizations to help veterans who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless.

President Trump and Republican leadership are delivering lower taxes for working families and family farms, major private investment and high-quality jobs, stronger rural healthcare, critical support for farmers, and real resources for veterans. Iowans now face a choice: continue this record of results that puts workers, seniors, farmers, and communities first — or return to the higher taxes, open borders, and failed policies that put America last.

  • Bigger Refunds: South Carolina taxpayers saw average refunds of $3,476 in 2026.
  • Protecting Jobs and Wages: The Working Families Tax Cuts safeguarded 86,000 South Carolina jobs, $15 billion in state GDP, and $8 billion in workers’ wages.
  • Opportunity Zones: In September 2026, Gov. Henry McMaster submitted South Carolina’s new Opportunity Zone nominations to the Treasury, made possible by the permanent extension of the program — unlocking new private capital and economic opportunity for communities statewide.

Strengthening Rural Healthcare Access

President Trump is delivering targeted resources to expand access and modernize care in South Carolina’s rural communities.

  • Rural Health Transformation: South Carolina secured $200 million in first-year funding through the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Rural Health Transformation Program.
  • Modernizing Care Delivery: In September, the state awarded $167.3 million in Rural Health Transformation Program grants to 228 rural providers for primary care, maternal care, pediatrics, and behavioral health — removing barriers and building long-term capacity through facility modernization, technology upgrades, and workforce development.

Unleashing Private Investment and Job Creation

President Trump’s pro-growth, America First agenda is driving major private investment and high-quality job creation throughout the Palmetto State.

  • NorthMark Strategies is committing $2.8 billion to build a high-performance computing center in Spartanburg.
  • Octapharma is investing $1.5 billion to construct a critical care manufacturing facility in Rock Hill.
  • Ferrara Candy Company is investing $675 million to establish its first South Carolina operation in Orangeburg County.
  • Okonite is investing $400 million to build a new high-voltage electric cable plant in Orangeburg, creating 105 jobs.
  • Eaton is investing $340 million to expand U.S. transformer production in Jonesville.
  • Scout Motors is investing $300 million to develop a Supplier Park at its Blythewood Production Center and seven of its suppliers are investing more than $82 million across Spartanburg, Duncan, and Piedmont.
  • Adeptus USA is investing $215.6 million to launch its first South Carolina operation in Anderson County, creating 217 jobs.
  • TS Conductor is investing $134 million to open an advanced manufacturing facility in Hardeeville.
  • AmbioPharm is investing $119 million to expand peptide manufacturing and development at its Aiken County facility.
  • Rolls-Royce is investing $75 million to expand its Aiken manufacturing facility.
  • Red Metals is investing $70 million to establish a copper manufacturing operation in Charleston County.
  • Century Aluminum Co. is investing $50 million to restore its Berkeley County plant to full capacity for the first time in a decade.
  • George Utz Inc. is investing $40 million to build its first South Carolina manufacturing facility in Sumter County.
  • Re:Build is investing $20 million to open an advanced composites plant for aerospace and defense products in Rock Hill.
  • Tyson Steel is investing $15.2 million to establish its first South Carolina operation in Pickens County.
  • Coastal Precast Systems is investing $9 million to relocate its operations to Laurens County.
  • UFP Packaging is investing $5.3 million to open a wood packaging plant in Gaffney.

Investing in South Carolina Communities

President Trump is delivering targeted federal resources that strengthen roads, military installations, disaster recovery, and educational opportunity.

  • Strengthening Roads and Bridges: In July 2026, the Trump Administration awarded South Carolina a $23.5 million grant to replace 18 aging bridges across nine counties.
  • Modernizing Military Installations: The FY 2027 NDAA authorized $161.7 million for a nuclear power training facility expansion at Joint Base Charleston and extended funding totaling $166.7 million for new recruit barracks at Parris Island.
  • Delivering Disaster Recovery: In October 2026, President Trump approved South Carolina’s request to raise the federal share of Hurricane Helene Public Assistance recovery costs from 75% to 90%.
  • Supporting HBCUs: In September 2026, the Trump Administration awarded nearly $10 million to eight South Carolina HBCUs, led by $2.4 million to South Carolina State.

Making South Carolina Safe Again

President Trump and Republicans are delivering results that reduce crime and restore safety for South Carolina families.

  • Violent crime fell 11% and property crime fell 14% last year, including sharp drops in murders (17%), robberies (19%), aggravated assaults (9%), and burglaries (15%).
  • In Charleston, overall crime plunged 36% in 2025, with homicides down 29%, aggravated assaults down 16%, robberies down 24%, and sex offenses down 39% from the five-year average.
  • At least 72 law enforcement agencies, including the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division and the South Carolina Department of Public Safety, have signed 287(g) agreements with ICE to identify, detain, and remove violent illegal alien criminals from the state.

President Trump and Republicans are delivering lower taxes, major private investment, stronger rural healthcare, critical infrastructure, and safer communities. South Carolinians face a clear choice: continue this progress, or return to the higher taxes, open borders, and failed policies of the past.
